Title: Director of Business Technology
Description:
Liteline Corporation is a privately held Canadian commercial lighting manufacturer with more than 160 employees, selling across Canada and the United States. We are adding a Director of Business Technology to our leadership team, a senior, hands-on role with ownership of technology across the business.

The role has two halves. The first is the job every growing company needs: keep our technology running, secure and recoverable across roughly 130 computers, Microsoft 365, our server cluster and our network. The second is newer. Our own people, from the three Co-Presidents to staff in Finance, Product Development, Engineering and Customer Service, now build software tools with AI assistants. The Director of Business Technology will give that work a professional backbone: version control, permissions, backups and fast recovery.

This is an enabling role as much as a technical one. We want our people to keep building quickly. The person in this position will make sure what they build is safe, recoverable and well looked after, without slowing anyone down.

This is a build role. Liteline’s people are already creating their own tools with AI. We are looking for a leader who can keep the core IT environment solid, put the right platforms and guardrails under home-built software, and teach non-programmers to work safely.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Keep Things Running**

* Own day-to-day IT across the business: computers, email, servers, networking, security and backups.
* Run Microsoft 365, including sign-in, multi-factor authentication (MFA), user access and licensing.
* Look after our on-premises server cluster, storage and network infrastructure.
* Oversee security monitoring and incident response together with our security monitoring partner.
* Maintain tested backups and the ability to restore systems and data quickly.
* Lead the help desk and set the service standards the business is held to.

**Own the Platforms**

* Set up and run, hands-on, the platforms our home-built tools live on.
* Own Liteline’s company GitHub organization, where code is saved with full history, including structure, permissions, single sign-on (SSO) and branch protection.
* Administer hosted databases (Supabase / Postgres), including access control, backups and recovery.
* Manage website and application hosting (Netlify), including deployments, domains and environments.
* Maintain a clear inventory of the tools in use, who owns each one and where it runs.

**Govern and Teach**

* Decide what AI assistants can access and set sensible guardrails for company data and credentials.
* Set light, practical rules that protect the business without getting in the way of the people building.
* Decide which home-built tools are business-critical and what level of protection each one needs.
* Run and rehearse restores so that recovery is proven, not assumed.
* Teach staff who are not programmers to work safely, for example explaining version control to someone in purchasing.
* Run training, enablement and “lunch and learn” sessions across the business.

**Team and Partners**

* Lead two on-site IT staff.
* Manage our outside partners for managed services, security monitoring and backup.
* Own the technology budget, licensing and vendor relationships, and bring forward stronger options as the market moves.

**WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR**

We are looking for a hands-on technology leader who is equally comfortable running core IT and building platforms that sit under modern, AI-assisted development.

The successful candidate will understand infrastructure, identity and security, and will also understand how software is built, saved, deployed and recovered. Just as importantly, you will be able to explain those ideas in plain language to people who have never written code and help them adopt habits that last.

**Strong candidates will bring:**

* Hands-on experience setting up or administering a GitHub organization, including SSO and branch protection.
* Experience running a Microsoft Power Platform Centre of Excellence, citizen-developer or low-code programme.
* Hands-on experience running Supabase, Postgres, Netlify, Vercel or similar platforms.
* Solid Microsoft 365, identity, MFA, endpoint and security fundamentals.
* A track record of training and enabling non-technical staff, such as “lunch and learn” or enablement programmes.
* Experience building a function or process from scratch at a growing company.
* Clear communication and sound judgment about when rules help and when they get in the way.

There is no single path to this role. You might be:

* An IT lead at a 100-to-500-person manufacturer or distributor who personally ran a Power Platform governance programme, a low-code programme or the company’s GitHub organization.
* A developer or DevOps engineer who moved into an IT management role at a small or mid-sized company.
* A solutions architect or senior consultant at a managed services provider (MSP) serving small and mid-sized businesses, ready to go in-house.
* The “first IT hire” at a startup who set up sign-in, devices and GitHub from scratch, then moved to a mid-sized company.
* Experience in mid-sized manufacturing, distribution or wholesale is helpful but not required.

**REPORTING AND WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

This position reports to the VP of Operations.

You will work closely with Liteline’s three Co-Presidents, who are technically capable and build their own tools, and with Finance, Product Development, Engineering and Customer Service. You will be a partner to the people building, not a gatekeeper.

**LOCATION AND WORKING ARRANGEMENT**

This position is based at Liteline's Richmond Hill head office and is on-site five days per week with regular presence at our distribution facilities.

The successful candidate should expect to be highly engaged with the business and to spend real time understanding how departments and facilities actually operate.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

This is a rare chance to shape how an established Canadian manufacturer builds and runs its technology at a moment when AI is changing who can create software.

Liteline is privately held, decisions are made without layers of approval, and good ideas get backed. Our leaders build with technology themselves and value this work. The Director of Business Technology will define the platforms, guardrails and habits that let the whole company build with confidence.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

Liteline offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental and life insurance following three months of service, and a group RRSP with partial company match.

**TO APPLY**

Qualified candidates are invited to apply directly through this posting.

*Liteline Corporation is an equal opportunity employer that values the unique skills and experiences of every candidate. We are committed to accommodating people with disabilities throughout the recruitment and hiring process. To request accommodation, please contact Human Resources with the position title in the subject line.*

Pay: $150,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Company events
* Disability insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Extended health care
* Life insurance
* On-site parking
* RRSP match
* Vision care

Application question(s):

* How many years of work experience do you have with IT Strategy?
* Have you built or significantly developed an IT, business technology, technology governance, or technology enablement function or process from the ground up?
* Do you have hands-on experience setting up or administering a GitHub organization, including SSO, permissions, branch protection or repository governance?
* Do you have hands-on experience administering Microsoft 365 environments, including identity, MFA, endpoint management, and security?
* Do you have hands-on experience administering or supporting platforms such as Supabase, PostgreSQL, Netlify, Vercel, or similar technologies?

Experience:

* IT: 7 years (required)
* DevOps: 3 years (required)
* Microsoft Platform: 3 years (required)

Work Location: In person

Title: Manager, Care Operations
Description:
**Overview**
Tonal Care runs seven days a week across an in-house Toronto team and an outsourced partner operation. The Manager, Care Operations owns how that operation performs day to day.
  
  
You will own daily delivery across all tiers, the operational relationship with our outsourced partner, and the staffing and capacity plans that keep service levels intact. You will lead a Team Lead and a team of Customer Experience Specialists, each of whom owns one or two lines of business, and you will work the queue yourself when coverage requires it.
  
  
This is a hands-on, player/coach, operating role. You set the standard, work within it, and hold the operation to it.
  
  
What You Will Do
  
  
Daily Delivery
  
  

* Act as a player-coach during the initial phase, spending dedicated time working directly in the queue alongside specialists to model best practices, coach in real time, and establish baseline workflows
* Own daily delivery across all tiers, setting service levels, coverage models, and workflow standards that hold consistent delivery across phone, email, chat, and video.
* Own the daily, weekly, and monthly plans for SLA, CSAT, Average Handle Time, and First Contact Resolution, and be accountable for hitting them.
* Identify performance trends, operational risks, and root causes, and build the action plans that close the gap.
* Lead regular performance reviews and operational business reviews with internal stakeholders and partner leadership.
* Support incident and volume management during elevated contact periods, product issues, launches, and other business disruptions.
* Work the queue yourself when coverage requires it — absences, PTO, peak volume, or an uncovered line of business. You are the final backstop on coverage.
* Translate operational data into clear insights and recommendations for Care leadership.

Outsourced Partner Performance
  
  

* Serve as the day-to-day operational point of contact for Tonal’s outsourced partner, managing performance through their team leads and supervisors.
* Hold partner leadership accountable to agreed KPIs, SLAs, quality standards, staffing commitments, and Tonal’s brand voice.
* Run weekly performance reviews with partner teams.
* Report weekly to our Logistics, Field Operations, and Care Leadership team across all Care Operations metrics.
* Partner with their leadership on performance improvement plans, staffing strategies, coaching opportunities, and operational readiness.
* Monitor partner staffing, attrition, attendance, and utilization to catch capacity risk before it reaches Members.
* Make sure partner teams are aligned to Tonal policies, workflows, and operating standards, and are prepared for new programs, product changes, and launches.
* Escalate to the Senior Manager, Care Operations when partner performance issues cannot be resolved at the working level. Contract terms, rates, and renewals sit with the Director of Care Operations.

Staffing and Capacity
  
  

* Own workforce planning with partner Workforce Management and Tonal analytics, setting capacity and staffing models against forecast demand and adjusting intraday to protect service levels.
* Plan coverage across the full seven-day operating window, including weekends, holidays, and peak periods.
* Own the volume, staffing, and partner utilization assumptions that feed Care’s operating budget.
* Monitor forecast accuracy and adjust staffing assumptions based on actual contact volume, productivity, shrinkage, and service-level performance.
* Ensure schedules keep the teams at a sustainable working load rather than at full utilization, so there is room to absorb spikes and absences.

Team Leadership
  
  

* Lead and develop the team through the Team Lead and senior specialists, owning performance calibration, coaching, career development, and coverage planning.
* Make sure every line of business has a named owner, that the assignment is understood, and that owners are held to how their domain performs.
* Be accountable for the escalations programme. Specialists and the Team Lead resolve individual escalations; you own how the programme performs and where it needs to change.
* Sit in the health, safety, and legal escalation chain: Specialist → Team Lead → Manager, Care Operations → Senior Manager, Care Operations → Director, Care Operations.
* Ensure clear ownership and communication on sensitive, complex, or high-risk Member situations.
* Monitor escalation trends to surface recurring Member pain points, and work with the frontline to reduce avoidable escalations and lift first contact resolution.

Process and Partnership
  
  

* Translate the operating plan set with the Senior Manager, Care Operations into daily execution, and own that execution.
* Work with the Care Enablement team to identify knowledge gaps and roll out new troubleshooting SOPs, training, and tool updates to the front line.
* Coordinate with Logistics and Field Operations to deliver a seamless end-to-end experience for both specialists and Members.
* Simplify workflows to reduce Member effort, improve specialist efficiency, and remove unnecessary operational friction.
* Represent Care Operations in cross-functional initiatives and launches, and support the rollout and adoption of new tools, processes, and support programs.

Coverage and Schedule
  
  
Tonal Care operates seven days a week, 9:00 AM to 10:00 PM EST. This is a hands-on leadership role and the coverage expectations come with it:
  
  

* You and your team may be required to work weekends, holidays, and after hours as coverage requires. You and your team’s schedule will shift with the needs of the operation.
* Your team will carry on-call responsibility for incidents, outages, product issues, and elevated volume periods.
* Priorities change during the day. Peak season, launches, and product escalations will change what a day looks like.

Who You Are
  
  

* You have 5+ years of experience in Customer Care, Customer Support, or Contact Center Operations, including 2+ years leading teams, vendors, or outsourced operations.
* You are operationally minded and move comfortably between the operating plan and the queue. You set the standard, then hold the operation to it.
* You have managed operational KPIs and used data to find and fix performance problems. You don’t just report numbers — you understand the why behind them and change process, staffing, or enablement to move the trend.
* You are an empathetic coach who knows how to motivate a team and can turn complex data into feedback a specialist can act on.
* You have handled complex escalations and high-impact customer situations, and you are comfortable navigating gray areas and making quick, sound decisions when they arise.
* You have strong vendor and stakeholder management skills, and can influence partners who don’t report to you.
* You are technically savvy and proficient in CRM and support tooling, with an understanding of how backend systems shape the frontline experience.
* You prioritize influence over authority, earning the trust of your team and stakeholders to drive results through collaboration rather than mandate.
* You are comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment with changing priorities and evolving processes.

Why You Will Love Working at Tonal
  
  

* You will own the operating model for a Care organization that is scaling across channels and lines of business
* Competitive compensation package, benefits, and Tonal product perks
* Collaborative, mission-driven team with a passion for redefining strength training

At Tonal, we believe that the unique and varied lived experiences of our teammates contribute to our overall strength. We don’t just appreciate differences, we celebrate them, and we always seek people that represent a wide variety of backgrounds. We’re dedicated to adding new perspectives to the team and designing employee experiences that contribute to your growth as much as you do to ours. If your experience aligns with what we’re looking for (even if you don’t check every single box), send us your application. We would love to hear from you!
  
  
Tonal is committed to meeting the diverse needs of people with disabilities in a timely manner that is consistent with the principles of independence, dignity, integration, and equality of opportunity. Should you have any accommodation requests, please reach out to us via our confidential email, accessibility@tonal.com. All requests will be addressed and responded to in accordance with Tonal’s Accessibility Policy and local legislation.
  
  
Compensation Range: CA$95K - CA$120K

Title: Market Operations Manager

Title: QNB3798 - Vice President IT Project Management (Qatarization)
Description:
**About QNB**
Established in 1964 as the country’s first Qatari-owned commercial bank, QNB Group has steadily grown to become the largest bank in the Middle East and Africa (MEA) region.
  
  
QNB Group’s presence through its subsidiaries and associate companies extends to more than 31 countries across three continents providing a comprehensive range of advanced products and services. The total number of employees is more than 28,000 serving up to 20 million customers operating through 1,000 locations, with an ATM network of 4,300 machines.
  
  
QNB has maintained its position as one of the highest rated regional banks from leading credit rating agencies including Standard & Poor’s (A), Moody’s (Aa3) and Fitch (A+). The Bank has also been the recipient of many awards from leading international specialised financial publications.
  
  
Based on the Group’s consistent strong financial performance and its expanding international presence, QNB currently ranks as the most valuable bank brand in the Middle East and Africa, according to Brand Finance Magazine.
  
  
QNB Group has an active community support program and sponsors various social, educational and sporting events.
  
  
**Job Purpose Summary**
The incumbent is primarily responsible for managing the day-to-day operational and tactical aspects of multiple or large scale IT projects. He is also responsible to set a plan to define the phases to be followed during the implementation of the agreed upon IT projects.
  
  
**Essential Duties & Responsibilities By Dimensions**
Continuous Improvement:
  
  

* Shareholder & Financial:
* Compare financial data for practice to that of other practices and seek ways to maximize revenue. Manage and achieve revenue goals set for projects.
* Implements KPI’s and best practices for VP IT Project Management
* Promote cost consciousness and efficiency and enhance productivity, to minimise cost, avoid waste, and optimise benefits for the bank.
* Act within the limits of the powers delegated to the incumbent and delegate authority to the respective staff and monitor exercise of the same.
* Demonstrate clear understanding of the important factors behind the bank's financial & non-financial performance.
* Customer (Internal & External):
* Maintain relations with the project recipient for progress reporting and project evaluation.
* Develop full scale project plans and associated communications documents
* Collects metrics data(such as baseline, actual values for costs, schedule, work in progress, and work completed) & reports on project progress and other project specific information to stakeholders
* To assist customers in all their queries on Bank’s product and seek solution to their requests.
* Maintain activities in accordance with Service Level Agreements (SLAs) with internal departments/units to achieve improvements in turn-around time.
* Build and maintain strong/effective relationships with related departments/units to achieve the Group’s objectives.
* Provide timely/accurate data to external/internal Auditors, Compliance, Financial Control and Risk when required.
* Internal (Processes, Products, Regulatory):
* Define portfolio goals to be achieved and measurement methods to track the achievement of the benefits.
* Oversees and develops project managers, senior project managers on stakeholder management, requirements management, resource management, project planning and project tracking.
* Handle situation escalations and provides the management skills and guidance required to achieve breakthroughs and removal of road-blocks to progress.
* Assist in preparing strategies, policies, standards and guidelines of project management and control to deliver the projects assigned objectives within the limited resources, time and budget.
* Controls and monitors “triple constraints”—project scope, time and cost(quality also)—in managing competing project requirements Handle multiple large and complex projects in parallel
* Effectively follow the Project Management Methodology while managing the projects
* Assist in creating project management methodologies for the implementation of all IT related projects within the Group.
* Approve the schedule of projects and work program of each project to be executed as per the budget and ensuring timely vendor selection/ procurement of equipment, hardware, software and various resources for the timely completion of projects.
* Direct the successful implementation of the project, including the restructuring of business processes and procedures to deliver efficient and effective operations while utilizing the capabilities of the new system.
* Review project design documents prepared by staff consultants and contractors and ensure they meet QNB and regulatory standards and quality expectations.
* Monitor the efforts of the project team to accomplish the project plan and take action as needed to resolve issues interfering with the successful completion of the project.
* Ensure that quality management is implemented in all IT processes.
* Conduct project risk analysis and maintain project risk profile.
* Identify, log, analyze and manage potential and actual issues and risks, and take corrective action by tackling day to-day issues head on, and review how more serious issues and risks might impact on scope, schedule, quality and cost.
* Assess the efficiency and the effectiveness of the project and system once implemented, taking appropriate steps to resolve any problems/ issue noted.
* Review and provide feedback on the performance of the project team and make recommendations as necessary.
* Set examples by leading improvement initiatives through cross-functional teams ensuring successes.
* Identify and encourage people to adopt practices better than the industry standard.
* Continuously encourage and recognise the importance of thinking out-of-the-box within the team.
* Encourage, solicit and reward innovative ideas even in day-to-day issues.

Title: Project Engineering Manager, Staff
Industry: Semiconductor Manufacturing, Software Development, and Computer Hardware Manufacturing
Description:
We Are
  
  
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
  
  
What You'll Be Doing
  
  

* Own and maintain the integrated schedule and critical path across multiple Memory Interface IP development and release workstreams, from project kickoff and architecture through design closure, verification, customer delivery, and production readiness. Model dependency chains deeply enough to quantify the impact of slips and pull-ins, distinguish paths with float from those without it, and update the plan weekly using current engineering data.
* Drive the weekly project cadence by synthesizing inputs from architecture, RTL, design verification, analog and mixed-signal design, physical design, packaging, software, infrastructure, product engineering, and post-silicon teams into a single view of program health, emerging concerns, and required actions.
* Track verification convergence and engineering maturity as leading indicators. Monitor feature readiness, RTL closure, bug discovery and closure trends, regression health, coverage, design maturity, and block-level readiness. Recognize when convergence is stalling and drive a recovery plan before downstream milestones or customer commitments are affected.
* Analyze schedule scenarios and coordinate recovery plans. Work with engineering leads to understand technical constraints, resource limitations, and available float; quantify the impact of changes; develop practical options; and track agreed recovery actions to closure.
* Manage external partner and customer dependencies by owning delivery calendars, tracking execution plans and acceptance criteria, aligning technical dependencies, and supporting schedule negotiations with a clear understanding of downstream technical, commercial, and resource impacts.
* Lead cross-functional risk, issue, and decision management. Convert technical uncertainty into clear options, owners, dates, and decision points. Ensure risks, assumptions, and trade-offs are visible early and resolved at the appropriate level.
* Provide concise project insight to executives and customers. Distill complex engineering information into evidence-based updates that distinguish signal from noise, quantify schedule and delivery impact, and clearly identify the actions or decisions needed.

A Day In The Life
  
  
You start the morning reviewing verification-convergence dashboards and regression results, spotting a block where bug-closure velocity has slowed. You bring the DV lead and RTL owner together for a focused sync, clarify the cause, and align on a recovery plan before the weekly project review.
  
  
In that review, you walk leadership through an updated critical path that reflects an internal delivery shift, quantify the downstream impact on release timing and customer commitments, and identify the decisions needed to protect the plan. Later, you follow-up with R&D on the strategy to take to resolve the issue, then finish the day preparing a concise executive summary and following up on owners and due dates from the project review.
  
  
What You'll Need
  
  

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Applied Science, Computer Science, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience, with 8+ years of relevant experience in semiconductor, silicon IP, SoC, ASIC, or complex hardware development.
* Demonstrated experience managing complex semiconductor or silicon IP programs across multiple engineering disciplines and geographically distributed teams.
* Strong working knowledge of semiconductor development lifecycles and the relationships among architecture, RTL, verification, analog and mixed-signal design, physical design, software, infrastructure, and productization.
* Demonstrated ability to build and maintain integrated schedules with meaningful dependency and critical-path modeling, including float analysis, milestone confidence, and the downstream effects of schedule changes.
* Experience using engineering evidence such as feature readiness, bug trends, regression results, coverage, design closure, and delivery health to assess schedule risk and drive corrective action.
* Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate complex technical and program information, develop practical options, and recommend a course of action.
* Strong communication and influence skills, including the ability to gain cooperation across engineering teams, customers, suppliers, and external partners and to present crisp status and recommendations to senior leadership.
* Experience with project and program management tools and data-driven reporting. Familiarity with Jira, schedule-management tools, dashboards, and engineering lifecycle metrics is preferred.
* Knowledge of quality-management processes and the ability to navigate Linux environments are considered assets.

Who You Are
  
  
This is not a status-reporting role. You will connect a broad set of engineering workstreams into a coherent, dependency-driven plan, identify the real critical path week to week, and drive the cross-functional actions and decisions that keep complex Memory Interface IP projects on track. The work spans concurrent development efforts with significant interdependencies across engineering disciplines, customers, external partners, and development infrastructure.
  
  
Working with general direction, you will apply strong semiconductor-development knowledge and program-management judgment to analyze issues, recommend practical solutions, and gain cooperation across teams. Success requires attention to engineering detail, disciplined follow-through, and the ability to turn complex technical inputs into clear priorities, ownership, and delivery commitments.
  
  
The Team You'll Be Part Of
  
  
Our engineering teams develop advanced Memory Interface IP that enables customers to build high-performance, differentiated SoCs. We work at the intersection of architecture, analog and mixed-signal design, RTL, verification, physical design, software, infrastructure, and customer deployment. The programs are technically complex, globally distributed, and tightly connected to customer and business commitments.
  
  
We value people who combine advanced technical judgment with clear communication, disciplined execution, and the willingness to work through details without losing sight of the broader outcome. In this role, you will help shape how complex semiconductor programs are planned and delivered, strengthen execution practices across teams, and work alongside talented engineers solving consequential problems at scale.
  
  
Rewards and Benefits
  
  
We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

We are committed to provide access & opportunity to individuals with disabilities and will provide reasonable accommodation to individuals throughout the recruitment and employment process. Should you require an accommodation, please contact hr-help-canada@synopsys.com.

### **Job Purpose**

The Head of U.S. Operational Technology (OT) is a senior leadership role accountable for the safe, reliable, resilient, secure and supportable operation of the technology environments that underpin real-time electric transmission, electric distribution and gas distribution operations across Massachusetts and New York. The role reports to the VP, Head of IT&D Electric and works in close partnership with Electric and Gas Operations, Cybersecurity, Engineering, Architecture, Regulatory, Capital Delivery and other enterprise technology leaders.

The role leads a multidisciplinary organization responsible for 24x7 operational support and lifecycle stewardship of OT applications and infrastructure. It also includes designated technology supporting LNG operations, physical security systems, substation controllers and substation access points.

You’ll join an established team, building on its existing strengths to deliver meaningful outcomes. Working collaboratively with colleagues and stakeholders, you’ll help shape priorities, improve ways of working, and support the team’s continued development and success.

The Head of OT leads directors responsible for application and infrastructure domains and is a key partner to control center, operations, regulatory and executive stakeholders. The role requires experienced, visible leadership during significant events; disciplined governance; strong technical judgment; and the ability to convert technical risk into clear business decisions.

### **Key Accountabilities**

**Safe, Reliable and Resilient Operations**

* Own the availability, resilience, performance, and recoverability of the OT estate.
* Establish clear 24x7 operational accountability, escalation, and decision-making.
* Lead technology response to major incidents and operational events.
* Maintain and test business continuity, disaster recovery, and recovery capabilities.
* Ensure readiness for storms, grid emergencies, outages, and critical operational events.
* Drive continuous improvement through incident analysis and root-cause elimination.

* Provide transparent reporting on operational, technology, and compliance risks.
* Support regulatory filings, rate cases, and investment planning.

* Drive risk-based management of patching, upgrades, vulnerabilities, capacity, and technical debt.
* Establish standards for integration, automation, observability, and platform management.
* Enable trusted operational data, analytics, and AI capabilities.

**Portfolio Prioritization and Investment Leadership**

* Lead transparent prioritization and resource trade-off decisions.
* Maintain credible operational and capital forecasts.
* Translate technology investments into measurable business outcomes.
* Ensure effective governance, intake, and decision-making processes.

**Enabling Capital Delivery and Operational Acceptance**

* Represent operational requirements throughout delivery and implementation.

* Identify and manage cross-program dependencies and risks.
* Enable smooth transition from project delivery to steady-state operations.

Title: Manager, Educational Technology
Description:
Reporting to the Director, Academic Quality and Teaching Innovation, the Manager, Educational Technology provides leadership and oversight vis-à-vis the SLATE (Sheridan's Teaching and Learning Environment) environment as well as broader educational technology strategy.

The incumbent is accountable for all operational aspects of SLATE, which operates for all Sheridan users on a continuous 24x7x365 basis. In this capacity the incumbent provides leadership for the administration, design, development, training, and support functions associated with SLATE as well as other integrated learning technologies, e-learning and digital innovation. This includes any internal integrations to Sheridan's infrastructure including but not limited to student information systems (SIS), HR systems, authentication services and other leveraged systems.

This position collaborates pan-institutionally to engage a wide range of key partners at Sheridan, i.e. Academic Division, IT, OTR, as it relates to planning, strategy, and operationalization of educational technologies, including but not limited to SLATE. The position engages and contributes to provincial and sector educational technology bodies. Further, the role is a key interface with educational technology vendors to ensure the provisioned tools are meeting the broader educational and pedagogical needs of the Sheridan teaching and learning community.

**What You’ll Be Doing**

* Managing system administration for SLATE and associated learning technologies, leading teams to improve the experience of faculty, students, and employees.
* Plans and assesses upgrades, patches, and pilots of new features; oversees the e-learning design and digital innovation teams; and advises the Director on the development and review of programs and services.
* Evaluating emerging technologies and, with the Director, builds business cases for adopting them, while managing the life cycle of learning technologies from onboarding to retirement.
* Managing major cross-College projects, supports budget and strategic planning, maintains policies, documentation, and usage statistics, and is accountable for timely, accurate communications.
* Managing vendor, sector, and internal partnerships through negotiating contracts, master agreements, SLAs, and End User License Agreements (EULA)s for all contracted services, including cloud-based services, and administers breach procedures such as responses to service disruptions.
* Maintaining relationships with account managers and other vendor representatives, stays apprised of product and service roadmaps, and leads vendor crisis management when service is disrupted or degraded.
* Providing leadership, strategic direction, and supervision to SLATE staff and other digital learning teams, ensuring adequate coverage, prompt response to user support requests, and proper escalation of issues to internal resources or vendors, with all issues documented and tracked to resolution.
* Hiring, supervising, coaching, and managing staff performance in compliance with the Collective Agreement, keeps certifications and training current, and recommends professional development aligned with Sheridan’s strategic vision, while fostering a safe, respectful, and inclusive work environment.
* Accountable for resource stewardship and compliance with Sheridan policies, legislation, and agreements, including Health and Safety, Human Rights, AODA, Acceptable Use, and WHMIS, as well as the secure management of records and confidential information under Sheridan’s Records and Information Management Policy.
* Ensuring the delivery of standard and ad hoc instructions and information on the use of learning technologies, including SLATE procedures, and prepares reports and presentations on SLATE, pilot projects, and other educational technologies for decision-making groups.
* Serves on committees and cross-organizational teams that need expertise in teaching and learning technology or input on SLATE implementation for other Sheridan initiatives, and represents the portfolio’s interests on institutional working groups such as legal, privacy, and web governance.
* Leads project teams, analyzing requirements, developing plans, scheduling resources, and tracking and reporting on deliverables to senior leadership.

You have a sound understanding of the **post-secondary education landscape**, including the challenges, emerging trends and issues shaping the sector, and can translate this knowledge into forward-thinking academic leadership.

You exercise sound **judgement**, and your strong **problem-solving and conflict resolution skills**, coupled with your openness to new ways of thinking, allow you to navigate complex challenges and develop creative solutions that advance organizational goals.

You demonstrate a strong understanding of **cultural diversity** and the varied experiences and needs of diverse populations and are committed to creating learning and working environments where individuals feel **welcomed, respected and supported**.

You demonstrate a strong commitment to **equity, diversity, inclusion and belonging** and to fostering an educational and employment environment that removes barriers and creates equitable opportunities for individuals to participate, contribute and succeed.

Title: Business Continuity Manager
Description:
**Position Summary**

The Business Continuity Manager is a key role responsible for overseeing the development and implementation of business continuity plans to ensure the company’s operations can withstand and recover from unexpected disruptions.

**What will your job entail?**

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Assess the potential impact of disruptions on critical business processes, identifying dependencies, recovery time objectives (RTOs), and resource requirements.
* Identify and evaluate risks that could affect business operations, including natural disasters, cyber threats, supply chain disruptions, and other emergencies. Develop strategies to mitigate these risks.
* Create and maintain comprehensive emergency response plans that outline procedures for handling crises, evacuations, communication, and resource allocation during disruptions.
* Develop and update business continuity plans (BCPs) that address various scenarios, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and compliance requirements.
* Coordinate regular testing and exercises to validate BCP effectiveness. Conduct tabletop simulations, functional exercises, and full-scale drills to assess readiness.
* Work closely with cross-functional teams, including IT, facilities, legal, and senior management, to ensure alignment and buy-in for business continuity efforts.
* Provide training sessions to employees on BCPs, emergency procedures, and their roles during disruptions. Foster a culture of preparedness and awareness.
* Regularly review and enhance business continuity strategies based on lessons learned, industry best practices, and changes in the business environment.  
    
  **Work Experience and Education:**
* Bachelor’s degree in Risk Management or Business with 6+ years of experience
* 3+ years of supervisor or lead experience.
* Insurance industry experience preferred

**Licenses &** **Certifications:**

Certified Business Continuity Professional (CBCP) or ISO 22301 Lead Implementer or Project Management Professional (PMP) is preferred

**Technical/Functional Skills:**

* Risk assessment and risk management: Identifies, analyzes, and prioritizes operational, technology, third-party, and environmental risks, and develops practical risk mitigation strategies aligned with enterprise risk management frameworks.
* Business impact analysis (BIA): Conducts BIAs to determine critical processes, dependencies, recovery time objectives (RTOs), recovery point objectives (RPOs), maximum tolerable downtime, and financial and operational impacts of disruption.
* Business continuity and resilience planning: Develops and maintains business continuity plans, crisis management and emergency response plans, and recovery strategies in line with ISO 22301, DRI International, or Business Continuity Institute (BCI) standards and practices.
* Strategic planning: Builds multi-year business continuity program roadmaps, defines program metrics, and aligns continuity priorities with business strategy and operational resilience goals.
* IT disaster recovery and technology resilience: Partners with IT and information security to align application recovery priorities, system dependencies, and disaster recovery capabilities with business recovery requirements.
* Third-party and vendor continuity: Evaluates the resilience of critical vendors, service providers, and delegated authority partners, including review of vendor continuity plans and recovery capabilities.
* Business continuity software administration: Administers and configures business continuity planning platforms to manage plans, BIAs, contact data, assessments, and reporting.
* Mass notification and threat intelligence administration: Manages emergency notification systems, including contact data quality, message templates, and delivery testing, and monitors threat intelligence sources to provide timely alerts on severe weather, safety, and other events affecting employees and operations.
* Exercise design and facilitation: Designs, facilitates, and documents tabletop, functional, and full-scale exercises, and tracks resulting corrective actions through to completion.
* Data analysis and reporting: Analyzes plan, exercise, and incident data to draw clear conclusions, and produces dashboards and metrics that inform decisions by leadership.
* Presentation development and delivery: Develops and delivers clear, concise presentations and training materials to audiences ranging from front-line employees to senior executives.

**Functional Requirements:**

* Own the enterprise business continuity program lifecycle, including governance, policy and standards, annual plan review and approval cycles, and program maintenance across all business units.
* Lead and maintain the BIA process for all business units, and ensure results drive recovery strategies, resource requirements, and plan content.
* Maintain business continuity, crisis management, and emergency response plans, and verify that plan owners review and update them at least annually and after significant organizational or operational change.
* Plan and execute an annual schedule of exercises and tests, and document results, gaps, and corrective actions with assigned owners and due dates.
* Coordinate the organization’s response during incidents and disruptions, including activating plans, convening the crisis management team, and supporting internal and external communications.
* Conduct post-incident and post-exercise reviews, and incorporate lessons learned into plans, training, and program improvements.
* Ensure the program meets applicable insurance regulatory, contractual, and audit requirements, such as state department of insurance expectations, NAIC guidance, and client or carrier due diligence requests.
* Support client, carrier, regulator, and auditor inquiries by providing business continuity attestations, evidence, and documentation.
* Report on program status, risks, exercise results, and key metrics to senior leadership, executive committees, and the board as required.
* Manage the business continuity planning and mass notification platforms, including user access, data accuracy, and regular testing.
* Develop and deliver business continuity awareness and training programs for employees, plan owners, and crisis management team members.
* Supervise or lead business continuity staff, contractors, and a network of plan owners and coordinators, setting priorities and providing direction and coaching.

**Behavioral Skills:**

* Effective communication: Communicates clearly and calmly in writing and verbally, tailoring messages for executives, technical teams, and employees, especially during high-pressure incidents.
* Interpersonal skills and influence: Builds trusted relationships and gains buy-in across departments, business units, and levels of leadership without relying on direct authority.
* Attention to detail: Maintains accurate, complete, and audit-ready plans, records, and contact data.
* Decision making: Makes timely, well-informed decisions with incomplete information and balances risk, cost, and operational impact.
* Problem-solving: Applies structured, analytical thinking to resolve complex issues and develop practical solutions.
* Leadership and accountability: Leads by example, follows through on commitments, and holds teams and plan owners accountable for deliverables.
* Continuous learning: Stays current on emerging threats, regulatory changes, and industry best practices, and applies new knowledge to improve the program.
* Emotional intelligence: Remains composed under pressure, shows empathy toward affected employees, and adapts communication style to different audiences and situations

Title: Director of Information Technology

* Establishes and reports on key performance indicators and service levels (e.g., response and resolution times, first-contact resolution, system availability, user satisfaction) to the CIO and Firm leadership.
* Builds a culture of high-touch client service, accountability, and continuous improvement within the IT department.

* Ensures reliable conference room, hybrid meeting, and trial and courtroom technology support.

**Legal and Business Applications**

**AI and Innovation**

* Contributes to the Firm’s AI governance efforts by supporting acceptable-use standards, data protection practices, vendor reviews, and the measurement of adoption and value.

**Cybersecurity, Risk, and Compliance**

* Partners with Information Security to implement and maintain security controls, including multi-factor authentication, endpoint detection and response, vulnerability and patch management, privileged access management, and data loss prevention.
* Supports client security audits and questionnaires, outside counsel guideline requirements, cyber insurance requirements, and alignment with frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, and NIST.

  **.**

* Performs other duties as assigned.

* Law firm or professional services experience strongly preferred (Am Law 200 preferred).
* Hands-on experience with Microsoft 365, Azure, Intune, and enterprise networking.
* Experience supporting legal applications such as document management, financial and practice management, and conflicts and intake systems.
* Proven track record leading enterprise technology projects (e.g., cloud migration, endpoint modernization, application upgrades).
* Experience managing IT budgets, vendor contracts, and IT asset management.

* Executive presence and the ability to build trusted relationships with partners and Firm leadership.
* Strong service orientation and commitment to excellence.

* Sound understanding of cybersecurity principles and controls.
* Excellent project management, organizational, and prioritization skills.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including explaining technical topics to non-technical audiences.
* Strong negotiation, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to manage conflict and maintain a positive, high-performance team environment.
* Ability to work under pressure, meet tight deadlines, and handle competing priorities.

* Ensure the accuracy and effectiveness of core operational processes, including reconciliation, corporate actions, fee administration, reporting, and portfolio administration.

* Collaborate with Advisors, Relationship Managers, Portfolio Services, Compliance, Risk, Technology, and other business partners to support operational excellence.
* Lead process improvement initiatives focused on automation, scalability, efficiency, and risk mitigation.
* Support regulatory requirements and ensure adherence to operational standards and governance frameworks.

Title: Senior Manager, Delivery Management
Description:
**\*\* This role is not eligible for sponsorship AND is four days onsite hybrid at our N. Scottsdale office \*\***

We're looking for a Senior Delivery Manager to help product teams ship with confidence by removing obstacles that slow them down, keeping dependencies from turning into surprises, and creating the conditions for them to stay focused on problem solving instead of fighting internal friction.

  

Delivery support may take several forms. You may maintain relationships within an assigned product area and shift your attention to teams where delivery support is useful; be temporarily aligned to a problem statement spanning multiple product teams or product groups; or support a mission team or High Integrity Commitment that requires more structured

coordination. In these assignments, you may apply program-management skills such as coordinating sequencing across workstreams, maintaining visibility into milestones and readiness, surfacing dependencies and risks, bringing the right decision-makers together, and driving agreed follow-through.

The best delivery managers are the ones who quietly prevent problems that never needed to happen (e.g., dependencies that get resolved before they derail, release processes that become routine, cross-team coordination that used to require six meetings and now take one).

You don't decide what gets built but make it possible for the Product team to build it well. You shape how product teams across the business unit deliver at scale — developing new approaches to systemic delivery challenges, influencing the organizational conditions that determine whether teams can sustain high performance, and driving delivery strategy across short to mid-term horizons.

You'll typically support multiple product teams or a complex product area, depending on scope and complexity. Your success is measured not only by whether teams deliver reliably, but whether the delivery strategy for the product area continuously evolves to meet short and mid-term business objectives and whether delivery practices you develop influence standards within your product area.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Remove impediments.** This is the job. You own complex impediments that span teams, product areas, stakeholders, or organizational boundaries. You look beyond the immediate blocker to identify systemic causes, working across product and engineering leadership to resolve issues that would otherwise continue affecting delivery. Where no established solution exists, you develop new approaches — and those approaches influence best practices.

**Manage dependencies across teams.** You lead coordination of complex dependencies spanning multiple teams or product areas, developing new coordination models where none exist, and influencing stakeholders to address the structural conditions that generate repeated dependencies. Your solutions are designed to last, not just to resolve the immediate situation.

**Support coordination for cross-team outcomes.** When assigned to a cross-product problem statement, mission team, or High Integrity Commitment, you make sequencing, milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions, communications, and readiness visible. Apply program-management skills within the agreed support scope without taking ownership of the product outcome, technical solution, integrated program, or accountable leaders’ commitments.

**Protect the team's focus.** You proactively navigate organizational complexity and remove unnecessary friction so teams can remain focused on discovery and delivery. You work directly with stakeholders when broader alignment, escalation, or decisions are required. You identify and influence changes to ways of working that impact delivery performance.

**Improve how teams deliver.** You contribute to new approaches to delivery improvement where existing methods fall short, and your recommendations shape delivery standards within your product area. Your work informs the strategy for how delivery gets done.

**Make work visible without creating overhead.** You ensure teams and leaders have meaningful visibility into delivery without creating reporting overhead. You use flow metrics and delivery data to identify trends across teams, distinguish isolated issues from systemic patterns, and provide data-backed recommendations to product and engineering leadership. Your analysis informs recommendations about resourcing and delivery investment that support short to mid-term planning horizons.

**Facilitate when facilitation adds value.** You don't own standup rituals or enforce ceremonies, but you can lead complex cross-team or stakeholder conversations when alignment, trade-offs, or decisions are preventing delivery from moving forward. You design and stand-up new forums when the organization lacks a mechanism to make critical, cross-cutting delivery decisions — and those forums outlast the immediate need.

**Lead delivery coordination for complex multi-team initiatives.** When delivery spans multiple teams or product areas, you establish the coordination approach, ensure risks and dependencies remain visible, and work with product and engineering leaders to resolve issues that threaten the broader outcome.

  

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

***Employment Experience***

  

* 10+ years in delivery or program management roles.
* Extensive experience supporting multiple concurrent product teams or a full product area, across multiple product areas within fast-paced software engineering organizations with demonstrated impact on business unit-level delivery strategy and outcomes.
* Deep experience operating within a product operating model or empowered product team environment; recognized as a primary resource on this way of working, with the ability to influence its adoption, evolution, and strategic direction within a product area.

**Technical Acumen**

  

* Solid understanding of software development processes and delivery terminology; ability to guide trade-off conversations across the full lifecycle, from discovery through release and production operations (no coding required). Your depth in this area is recognized in the organization and is applied to inform decisions about delivery investment.
* Fluency across multiple iterative and continuous-delivery models (Scrum, Kanban, Scrumban, etc.).
* Advanced proficiency in Jira and Confluence, including the ability to define cross-team workflow, reporting, telemetry, and automation requirements that improve delivery visibility and flow.

***AI & Agentic Delivery Practices***

  

* Everyday AI tools: Claude, Microsoft Copilot, and ChatGPT; ability to champion adoption of these tools, including coaching other Delivery Managers on effective day-to-day use.
* Solid understanding of AI-enabled and agentic delivery practices; demonstrated ability to use AI to improve delivery operations, identify opportunities where AI or automation could remove friction, coach other Delivery Managers and Product Teams on effective adoption, and build agents that create measurable value across a product area.
Working knowledge of AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) approach, including the ability to help evolve the methodology, surface recurring gaps or adoption barriers, and its guardrails as it matures.  

  

***Delivery Rigor, Lean Process & Flow Metrics***

  

* Ability to establish lightweight but disciplined practices for risk and dependency tracking across multiple teams or a product area, ensuring a single source of truth for delivery status without reintroducing PMO-style governance. Recognized as a primary resource on delivery rigor, with frameworks and approaches you develop adopted as standards.
* Track record of leading lean/continuous improvement initiatives and establishing lightweight delivery practices, operating rhythms, and flow metrics (cycle time, throughput, work in progress, flow efficiency) that drive measurable outcomes across multiple teams or a product area. Demonstrated ability to connect delivery performance data to recommendations that influence team investment and design decisions.
* Ability to build data-backed recommendations rather than relying on assumptions (e.g., "based on the last six weeks of data, flow continues to decrease during QA testing, indicating..."), validating with peer Delivery Managers across other product teams whether a pattern is isolated or systemic before escalating, and recognizing when issues trace back to a shared root cause worth fixing once for several teams at a time.

***Additional Skills & Competencies***

  

* You've built credibility as a delivery partner within empowered product teams. Product and engineering teams seek your perspective because you understand both how individual teams deliver and how organizational conditions affect their ability to do so. You are recognized within the organization as a primary resource on delivery practices, and you actively develop your knowledge of emerging practices in the field
* You've removed complex impediments spanning teams and organizational boundaries. You recognize when multiple delivery problems share the same underlying cause and know how to bring the right people together to solve it at the appropriate level. When no established approach exists, you create one — and it influences best practices.
* You understand software delivery deeply enough to facilitate delivery and trade-off conversations across the full lifecycle with engineering and product leaders, from discovery through release and production operations. Your depth of knowledge in this area is applied to inform recommendations that affect mid to short-term delivery investment and decisions.
* You have a low tolerance for meetings that don't change outcomes, reports nobody reads, and rituals that exist because "that's how we do it." If a process isn't serving the team, you say so. You work with stakeholders to remove or redesign departmental ways of working that limit delivery performance.
* You operate with some autonomy and exercise sound judgment independently in complex or ambiguous situations. You understand when delivery support should intensify, shift, or conclude. You can distinguish routine coordination from a systemic or material delivery risk, define an appropriate intervention, clarify decision and accountability boundaries, and avoid creating permanent governance around temporary delivery needs.
* You are always asking the question, what does the team need to deliver more effectively? You apply that thinking to what a product team or area needs to change so teams can deliver more effectively and provide recommended solutions on how to make that happen.
* You're a recognized delivery resource and coach. Other Delivery Managers and product and engineering teams seek your perspective on complex delivery challenges, and you help strengthen delivery practices beyond the teams you directly support.
* You're there to help the team deliver — they own their own commitments; you know how to shift from governing delivery to enabling it.

***Collaboration & Communication***

  

* Skill in leading multiple large-scale, concurrent initiatives and senior stakeholder relationships simultaneously without dropping detail; ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to synthesize complex, technical topics into clear, executive-ready materials. Ability to frame delivery strategy in terms of business unit impact, influencing decisions within a product area.
* Strong leadership presence; ability to influence without authority, lead stakeholder forums, mentor/coach other Delivery Managers, and work with cross-functional partners to unblock departmental-level issues and keep delivery moving across multiple teams or a product area.

***Education Requirements***

Bachelor's degree required.

**This Isn't the Right Fit If…**

If your experience is primarily in a PMO that governs delivery through stage gates, status reports, and resource allocation, be prepared for a fundamentally different dynamic. You won't be assigning work, approving plans, or tracking teams against committed roadmaps. The teams own their own commitments. You're there to help them get unstuck and move delivery forward.

If your instinct when something goes wrong is to add process, oversight, or governance rather than identify and remove the obstacle preventing progress, you'll struggle here.

This is not a role centered on Agile ceremony facilitation. This role is centered around cross-team coordination, delivery process improvement, navigating organizational complexity, and removing organizational impediments. At this level, it is also centered on influencing conditions and strategic decisions that determine whether delivery can succeed within a product area.

If you want to be involved in product decisions, that's a product management role, not this one. Senior Delivery Managers lead targeted interventions and complex coordination without replacing the leaders accountable for outcomes, technical decisions, organizational priorities, or commitments.

**In Your Application, Tell Us About…**

**A significant impediment you removed for a product team.** What was blocked, what did you do, and what would have happened if you hadn't intervened? How did your approach create a lasting solution that prevented the same category of problem from recurring within your product area?

**How you've managed a cross-team dependency.** What made it hard, and how did you make it work without turning it into a bureaucratic process? How did the coordination model you developed become a reusable approach that influenced how to manage future dependencies?

**A delivery process you improved within a team or product area.** What was broken, what did you change, and how did it affect the team's ability to ship? How did that improvement inform delivery standards within your immediate product area?

**A time you pushed back on unnecessary process or governance.** What was being asked of the team, why was it wasteful, and what happened when you challenged it? How did your pushback result in a lasting change rather than a one-time exception?

**Senior Delivery Managers at this level are recognized as skilled delivery professionals whose impact extends beyond the teams they directly support. Compensation reflects both team-level effectiveness and the product area influence this role brings to delivery strategy.**

We will lead with our values and act with care, compassion, and kindness. By doing this, we will Change Lives Together, every day and everywhere.

**ROLE SUMMARY**

For a scaling business that is preparing to enter a phase of growth, an effective and efficient program management office (PMO) is essential. Project management at Nando's has been strategically embedded into key disciplines: construction administration, technology enablement, and enterprise delivery. These three PMs work together in close coordination to drive our business priorities ahead and land them brilliantly.

As the principal technology delivery PM and key member of the USA Technology organization, you will work closely with the MD of Tech Enablement and key business partners both in the USA and around the Nando's World (UK, South Africa, Australia) to execute the USA Technology Roadmap and ensure flawless rollouts and execution in-restaurant. Most major technology initiatives require strong coordination and precise operational execution. You will be responsible to think quickly, be creative, remove blockers, and drive our tech agenda forward to deliver cutting edge solutions for our customers and teams. You will need to take a restaurant first approach to technology – listening to our operators, addressing their concerns and managing issues as they arise – by finding creative solutions to real-time challenges.

**CORE FOCUS AREAS**

*Administer the Nando's USA Technology Roadmap*

The first horizon (est. 12-18 months) USA Technology Roadmap has been established and kicked off. You will take over responsibility for administering execution, managing schedule, budget, dependencies, and risks across the +/- 12 interdependent workstreams.

*Drive Operations Adoption and Exceptional Delivery/Execution in Restaurants*  
You will be an Operations business partner and be responsible for working directly with the USA Ops Director and Market Managing Directors to align schedule/delivery with operational readiness and execution. You will serve as the technology liaison to Operations and ensure the field is ready for implementations.

*Monitor Budget and Schedule Considerations, Dependencies, and Risk Factors*

Working closely with the MD Technology and your finance business partner, you will oversee the technology department budget. You will be responsible for aligning capex requests to expected spend periods and monitoring accruals/rollover. You will report on budget status and re-forecast for accuracy and schedule alignment.

*Represent Technology within the USA Enterprise Flight Plan Delivery + Implementation Group*

You will be the voice of Technology within the USA Enterprise Flight Plan working group. You'll report tech initiatives out to the broader organization and ensure tech milestones/dependencies/conflicts are accurately surfaced and resolved.

*Balance Bold Ambition with Practical Realities*  
You will be on the front line of an ambitious agenda. Your role will be to balance aggressive ambition with practical reality and ensure the field and your counterparts are ready for the change before it hits. You'll chart out the direction of travel with the tech team and ensure it's clearly communicated across the business.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Build a nimble rollout/delivery infrastructure. Agree the scope, budget, and measures of success. Group restaurants into rollout waves that account for trading patterns, equipment lead times, engineer availability and dependencies between teams. Create the tools and materials needed to replicate rollouts well across the business.
* Connect the plan to the field. Coordinate site surveys with Operations and installation partners where required. Turn the findings into a plan for each restaurant, confirming what needs to be ordered, configured or resolved before engineers arrive. Ensure comms plans are market-specific and that the field remains informed and aligned with approach.
* Manage suppliers and logistics. Coordinate hardware procurement, deliveries and engineer bookings so the right people and equipment arrive at the right restaurant. Track supplier commitments and arrange the collection and processing of replaced hardware.
* Own change control around live trading. Agree installation windows with restaurant teams, including overnight work where needed. Before work starts, confirm who can authorize the change, how engineers and operating teams will test it, and when to switch to the fallback plan if trading is at risk.
* Manage the budget and report progress. Track purchase orders, actual spend and forecasts. Give stakeholders a clear view of which restaurants are ready, where costs or dates are at risk and which decisions need their attention.
* See each installation through to handover. Agree what a successful installation looks like with the restaurant manager and support teams. Confirm the equipment works in service, agree who owns support after go-live and make sure operating teams know how to get help. Give outstanding issues a defined owner and follow them through to resolution.
* Continually improve. Use feedback from restaurant teams and engineers to refine surveys, installation instructions and scheduling. Where an issue causes delays or repeat visits, address the cause before the next wave.

**SUCCESS CRITERIA**

Success in this role means:

* The Nando's USA technology roadmap is accurately managed, executed, and delivered  
  against the desired time horizons.
* Leadership has one integrated view of priorities, capacity, risks, and dependencies in the technology space, and uses it to make resourcing decisions.
* Strategic initiatives are delivered on time and within scope, with benefits tracked and reviewed after launch.
* Critical rollouts and systemwide tech delivery projects move through a clear, repeatable execution path.
* Technology is viewed as a center of excellence for Nando's USA and is an accelerator to our success. You deliver exceptional implementations without friction or frustration and work with your partners to continually improve.

Requirements:

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* 5–7 years of relevant experience in technology project management, technology delivery, or complex cross-functional implementations.
* Experience personally leading a technology rollout across multiple live locations from planning and procurement through to implementation and handover. Your background could be in hospitality, retail, banking branches or another environment where teams need to keep serving customers through a change.
* Experience managing technology changes in a live, customer-facing environment. You've agreed change windows with operational teams, coordinated technical and user testing, and put a workable fallback in place. You've also agreed who takes ownership after go-live and followed outstanding issues through to resolution.
* Experience coordinating third-party suppliers, field engineers and equipment logistics across several locations. You can recognize when a site isn't ready, bring the right people together and adjust the plan before an engineer is dispatched.
* Confidence managing project budgets, forecasting costs and explaining the options when dates, resources or supplier commitments change.
* Clear, considerate communication. You can give a busy restaurant manager the information they need for tomorrow's opening and help senior stakeholders make a timely decision about the wider rollout.
* Experience with core restaurant technology, including point of sale (POS) hardware and software systems, kitchen management systems (KMS), payment terminals, restaurant-specific hardware and software tools, etc. We're particularly interested in hearing about a rollout you owned, the decisions you made and how you knew the teams using the technology were ready to take it on.

**WORK ARRANGEMENT**  
This role is based in Washington, D.C. and requires a strong in-person presence to lead cross functional collaboration, mentor teams, and engage directly with key stakeholders.

**YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS**

The first 90 days of your employment will be a mutual onboarding and learning period, where both you and Nando's ensure you are set up for success in the role and that expectations are clear and aligned. We'll connect regularly to review progress, provide support, and ensure you have what you need to succeed. Employment with Nando's always remains at-will.

At Nando's, we believe in offering competitive pay that reflects the value you bring, the impact you'll  
make on our team, and the local market.
