Title: Physical Security Manager
Description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

OUR MISSION

True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

OUR VALUES

* **Be the offset.** We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.
* **What would it take?** We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.
* **It’s the people.** Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

BENEFITS & PERKS\*

* **Best-in-class healthcare:** 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents, with HSA/HRA options
* **Generous time off:** Flexible Time Off (FTO) for exempt employees, accrued PTO of up to 25 days for non-exempt employees, plus 12 paid holidays; Parental Leave; Sick Leave
* **Fuel for your day:** Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks for in-office employees
* **And more:** 401(k) retirement plan, fitness reimbursement, and Dog Fridays
* **Equity participation:** Equity is included as part of our total compensation package, giving you an opportunity to share in the company’s success.

* Do not apply to fixed term and temporary roles

YOUR MISSION

As Physical Security Manager, you will lead enterprise physical security across True Anomaly facilities and help deliver secure spaces that support our missions. You will protect people, property, and sensitive information by establishing consistent standards, coordinating guard services, and managing physical security systems and vendors.

You will lead security requirements and delivery coordination for Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) and open storage area (OSA) buildouts. Working with site Facility Security Officers (FSOs), Facilities, program teams, and government stakeholders, you will carry projects from planning and design through inspection, approval support, and turnover to site operations.

  

RESPONSIBILITIES

  

* **Enterprise physical security:** Develop and maintain standards for access control, intrusion detection, video surveillance, visitor management, keys and locks, opening and closing procedures, and protection of company assets.

* **Risk assessments:** Assess existing sites and proposed facilities; identify vulnerabilities, prioritize improvements, and communicate residual risks and resource needs to leadership.

* **Guard force coordination:** Establish service expectations, post order standards, training requirements, and performance measures. Partner with site FSOs and guard vendors on coverage, incident escalation, operating consistency, and corrective actions.

* **Security systems:** Own functional requirements and lifecycle planning for electronic security systems. Coordinate installation, commissioning, acceptance testing, preventive maintenance, repairs, and service agreements with qualified providers and IT.

* **Secure area buildouts:** Lead security scope and design reviews for SCIFs and OSAs, applying the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), Intelligence Community Directive 705 (ICD 705), and customer requirements as applicable.

* **Construction delivery:** Partner with Facilities and construction teams on security drawings, specifications, vendor scopes, budgets, schedules, and change reviews. Resolve security deficiencies and track dependencies that affect occupancy or classified operations.

* **Construction security:** Provide enterprise guidance to designated Site Security Managers (SSMs) on construction security plans, access controls, inspection records, and project documentation; identify needs for dedicated surveillance or escort support.

* **Technical coordination:** Coordinate applicable alarm certification, monitoring, acoustic protection, and government-directed TEMPEST or radio-frequency countermeasures with qualified specialists and the responsible government authorities.

* **Approval and accreditation support:** Coordinate required SCIF and OSA submissions, testing, inspections, and corrective actions with site FSOs, program security personnel, and the appropriate approving authorities.

* **Operational turnover:** Deliver security system records, as-built documentation, maintenance plans, operating procedures, and user training to site teams before transitioning completed projects into routine operations.

* **Vendors and budgets:** Develop statements of work, evaluate proposals with Procurement, monitor service quality and spending, and recommend investments based on mission needs and risk.

* **Incidents and improvement:** Coordinate physical security incident response and emergency planning with site teams and Facilities. Track system availability, guard performance, inspection findings, and improvement actions; coach site personnel on enterprise standards.

QUALIFICATIONS

* Seven or more years of relevant physical, industrial, military, or government security experience, including at least two years leading physical security initiatives or secure construction projects.

* Demonstrated experience delivering SCIF or OSA construction, renovation, or major modification projects and working with government security representatives.

* Working knowledge of NISPOM requirements, ICD 705 and its applicable technical specifications, and the processes used to obtain secure facility approvals.

* Practical experience with access control, intrusion detection, video surveillance, guard operations, and security vendor management.

* Ability to review construction drawings, define requirements, manage competing priorities, and communicate clear decisions to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

* Active U.S. Top Secret clearance and ability to obtain and maintain Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access. U.S. citizenship is required for this cleared role.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

An ideal candidate will also have:

* Experience supporting multiple facilities and building repeatable security processes in a growing aerospace or defense company.

* Prior SSM experience and formal training in secure facility construction or construction security.

* Familiarity with UL 2050 alarm certification and monitoring, acoustic testing, and coordination of government-directed TEMPEST requirements.

* Experience with Avigilon or comparable access control and video platforms, enterprise visitor management, and security service contracting.

* A relevant degree or professional credential, such as Certified Protection Professional (CPP), Physical Security Professional (PSP), or Project Management Professional (PMP). Current SCI access is preferred.

  

WHAT WE OFFER

* Collaborative, mission-focused culture with talented colleagues
* Competitive compensation package including base salary, equity, and performance bonuses
* Comprehensive benefits including health, dental, vision, 401(k) with match
* Professional development and training opportunities
Relocation assistance available for qualified candidates  
* ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

* **Travel:** Domestic travel to other company locations, construction projects, government offices, and vendor sites is required as business needs dictate.

* **Schedule:** Participate in coordinated after-hours support for security incidents, system outages, and critical construction activities.

* **Work environment:** Work in office, manufacturing, and active construction environments. Conduct site walkthroughs and inspections and follow applicable safety and personal protective equipment requirements, with reasonable accommodation as needed.
* **Work location:** Full-time, onsite position based in Denver, CO or Long Beach, CA. #LI-Onsite
  

COMPENSATION

* **Base Salary:** Denver - $120,000 - $175,000, Long Beach - $125,000 - $185,000
* **Equity + Benefits** including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave
* *Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, location, and experience.*

Title: Environmental Project Manager: State Cleanup Program
Description:
Date Posted: Nov 25, 2026

Requisition ID: 487073

Location:
Indianapolis, IN, US, 46204

**Work for Indiana**
====================

Begin a fulfilling career with the State of Indiana by joining one of the largest employers in the state, offering a range of opportunities across 60+ agencies. At the state, you'll find competitive compensation, a robust benefits package and a commitment to work-life balance. Most importantly, you'll have the chance to make a real and measurable impact on the lives of Hoosiers across Indiana.

**About Indiana Department of Environmental Management (IDEM):**

Our mission is to implement federal and state regulations to protect human health and the environment while allowing the environmentally sound operations of industrial, agricultural, commercial, and governmental activities vital to a prosperous economy. We issue air, water, and solid and hazardous waste permits that restrict discharges to environmentally safe levels. Staff members inspect and monitor regulated entities; provide compliance and technical assistance; monitor and assess air, land, and water quality; use enforcement actions as necessary to ensure compliance; and respond to incidents involving spills to soil or waters of the state.

**Role Overview:**

This position acts as the Project Manager managing administrative and technical oversight for remediation of hazardous substance and petroleum sites regulated by the Indiana Department of Environmental Management’s State Cleanup Program under the State of Indiana's Hazardous Substance and Petroleum cleanup laws. The position reports directly to the Section Chief for the program. Project managers are expected to develop project goals and timelines, and work in conjunction with technical support staff, legal counsel and IDEM Management to ensure that cleanups are conducted following appropriate IDEM agency guidelines and State and Federal laws.

**Role Responsibilities:**

The essential functions of this roles are as follows:

* Determines external parties legal responsibility for conducting necessary remediation action under State and Federal environmental law
* Determines goals and timelines for completion of each project
* Evaluates in-depth technical plans and reports concerning investigation and remediation of releases of hazardous substances and petroleum
* Coordinates with IDEM management, legal counsel and technical support staff as required to complete project goals and objectives
* Communicates clearly and concisely with external parties on their required responsibilities and timelines to complete project goals and objectives
* Tracks project milestones and metrics to ensure timely project completion
* Determines completeness of project tasks and recommends project closure as consistent with IDEM policies
* Conducts field oversight and sampling of environmental media as required
* Tracks expenditures, cost-recovery invoicing and conducts contracting as needed

  

**What We're Looking For:**

Two years or more work experience in an environmental or environmental public health field or a combination of accredited college degree and work experience in a related field. Accredited college degree in Biology, Chemistry, Environmental Science/Policy or Environmental Engineering.

**Working Conditions:**

This role performs work in a standard office environment and in the field with travel to project sites as needed. May include extended hours in the field. A flexible schedule is available to accomodate for work hours beyond normal schedule and personal scheduling.

**Salary:**

The salary for this position traditionally starts at $53,222.00 but may be commensurate with education and work experience. Use our **Compensation Calculator** to view the total compensation package.

**A Day in the Life:**
----------------------

The essential functions of this role are as follows:

**Environmental Technical Advisory & Program Support**

* Serves as an environmental expert and provides guidance to regulated communities, government officials, attorneys and staff responsible for a variety of programs and program elements.
* Conducts technical analysis and/or provides technical insights to assess environmental impacts with goals to meet state and national regulations.
* Provides technical and regulatory guidance to the regulated community in their assigned geographic area.
* Performs project management duties to ensure effective and timely management of program area needs, attends meetings, and responds to telephone calls, e-mails, etc., as required. Acts as a technical point-of-contact for assigned programs administering environmental programs which may include, but not limited to, environmental media sampling, data analysis, technical writing, work plan and report preparation, technical reviews, etc.
* Works to support the various programs in assigned agency in multiple capacities.

**Permitting & Regulatory Review**

* Researches state and federal guidance, laws, and regulations related to permits. Contacts applicants to request additional information to process applications, when necessary. Responds to comments from applicants, defends permit terms and conditions, and interacts with permittees to resolve permitting issues. Attends and participates in public meetings and hearings regarding permit actions throughout Indiana and/or appears in legal appeals of permit actions.

**Regulatory Compliance & Field Operations**

* Conducts surveys, inspections and investigations of facilities and sites, review projects/situations, reads plans, interprets findings, and cites appropriate violations of state and federal regulations. Provides technical and regulatory guidance to the regulated community in their assigned geographic area.
* Uses all compliance, enforcement tools, and resources available to ensure that regulated sources return to compliance with state and federal laws, regulations, and standards in a timely manner.
* Assists with the preparation of sampling and analysis work plans. Conducts field work as necessary following agency/section Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for assigned sites.
* Communicates effectively with responsible parties, consultants, and/or their representatives, affected stakeholders, and interested parties such as citizens, public officials, and interest groups in a courteous and professional manner regarding permits, laws, questions, and program-related inquiries.

The position involves routine travel to conduct inspections, investigations, and field reporting at regulated sites. Work hours may vary to meet operational demands and ensure efficient completion of assignments. The employee attends occasional meetings or events at the agency office.

The job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

This position is exempt from overtime compensation for additional work hours which may be required to complete essential functions or other assigned work. Exempt employees may work more than 75 hours in a pay period without additional compensation and must report a minimum of 75 hours per pay period of work hours and/or paid leave taken to receive their base biweekly salary.

**What You'll Need for Success:**
---------------------------------

Individuals in this role should minimally be able to articulate or demonstrate the following:

* Broad knowledge of theories, environmental protection principles and practices, specialty area, and program area.
* Thorough knowledge of chemistry, biology, hydrology, mathematics, engineering, and other environmental sciences as they relate to program area.
* Thorough knowledge of soil, water, air sampling, laboratory analysis and interpretation as it relates to program area.
* Ability to conduct surveys, inspections and investigations of facilities and sites, review projects/situations, read plans, interpret findings, and make recommendations.
* Ability to prepare documents for administrative and regulatory action.
* Excellent research and writing skills for preparing accurate, precise, clear, and thorough reports.
* Ability to effectively interact and orally communicate with parties with diverse levels of environmental expertise particularly for purposes of meetings, hearings, and negotiating critically sensitive issues.
* Ability to interpret and apply legal terminology and practices, and the ability to apply these in a variety of conditions and situations.

**A degree is not required. However, at least five (5) years of environmental or environmental public health experience applying the outlined knowledge, skills, and abilities in a similar role may be considered.**

Individuals should have the ability to perform essential functions with or without reasonable accommodation.

**Supervisory Responsibilities/Direct Reports:**
------------------------------------------------

This role may be utilized in a supervisory capacity based on agency needs.

The State of Indiana offers a comprehensive benefit package for full-time employees which includes:

* Three (3) medical plan options (including RX coverage) as well as vision and dental plans
* Wellness Rewards Program: Complete wellness activities to earn gift card rewards
* Health savings account, which includes bi-weekly state contribution
* Deferred compensation 457(b) account (similar to 401(k) plan) with employer match

* A robust, comprehensive program of leave policies covering a variety of employee needs, including but not limited to:
  + 150 hours of paid New Parent Leave and up to eight weeks of paid Childbirth Recovery Leave for eligible mothers
  + Up to 15 hours of paid community service leave
* Combined 180 hours of paid vacation, personal, and sick leave time off

* Education Reimbursement Program
* Group life insurance
* Referral Bonus program
* Employee assistance program that allows for covered behavioral health visits
* Qualified employer for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program
* Free Parking for most positions
Free LinkedIn Learning access

Title: System Director of Technology Operations and Governance
Description:
Pay Range:$75.26 - $105.59 The System Director, Technology Operations & Governance provides enterprise leadership and operational accountability for technology operations, service delivery, information security operations, technology project and portfolio performance, vendor management, service management, major incident coordination, and continuous improvement. The position ensures technology services are reliable, secure, responsive, financially responsible, and aligned with organizational priorities and the needs of clinical, operational, and administrative stakeholders.
  
  
Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the System Director leads a multidisciplinary portfolio that includes Help Desk leadership and support personnel, Information Security Operations leadership and staff, and IT Vendor Management staff. The position establishes operating standards, governance practices, performance measures, escalation paths, decision rights, and accountability across these functions.
  
  
Serves as the CIO's designated operational leader and strategic partner for enterprise technology governance, service delivery, information security operations, portfolio performance, and vendor management activities. As a senior member of the Information Technology leadership team, the position translates strategy into disciplined execution, supports executive decision-making, and provides leadership continuity for day-to-day technology operations.
  
  
SEARHC is a non-profit health consortium which serves the health interests of the residents of Southeast Alaska. We see our employees as our strongest assets. It is our priority to further their development and our organization by aiding in their professional advancement.
  
  
Working at SEARHC is more than a job, it’s a fulfilling career. We offer generous benefits, including retirement, paid time off, paid parental leave, health insurance, dental, and vision benefits, life insurance and long and short-term disability, and more.
  
  
**Key Essential Functions And Accountabilities Of The Job**
**Strategy, Executive Leadership, and CIO Partnership**

* Serve as the CIO's designated operational leader and strategic partner for enterprise technology governance, service delivery, information security operations, portfolio performance, and vendor management activities.
* Translate organizational and IT strategy into operating plans, priorities, resource requirements, performance expectations, and measurable outcomes.
* Advise the CIO and executive leadership on operational performance, information security priorities, portfolio health, vendor exposure, service capacity, and investment priorities.
* Prepare executive briefings, governance materials, business cases, risk summaries, budget recommendations, and decision requests.
* Represent Information Technology in enterprise governance forums and act on behalf of the CIO for assigned operational matters.

**Enterprise Technology Operations and Service Delivery**

* Lead enterprise technology operations and assigned service-delivery functions across all organizational locations and supported users.
* Establish IT service-management standards, operating procedures, service ownership, escalation paths, and performance expectations.
* Oversee major incident coordination, executive escalation, service restoration, root-cause review, corrective actions, and communications.
* Ensure operational readiness for implementations, upgrades, major changes, and transitions from project delivery into sustainable support.
* Maintain dashboards addressing demand, capacity, service levels, recurring issues, risks, customer experience, and improvement priorities.

**IT Service Desk and End-User Support**

* Lead Help Desk and assigned end-user support functions, ensuring timely, effective, courteous, and consistent service.
* Establish and monitor service-level expectations, customer satisfaction, first-contact resolution, backlog health, response time, resolution time, and escalation quality.
* Improve intake, triage, assignment, knowledge management, self-service, automation, communications, and request-fulfillment workflows.
* Use performance data and customer feedback to drive problem management, training, standardization, automation, and continuous improvement.

**Information Security Operations**

* Provide leadership and administrative oversight for assigned Information Security Operations personnel and security operations capabilities.
* Coordinate security monitoring, threat detection, incident response, vulnerability management, identity and access operations, security tooling, regulatory readiness, operational risk management, and performance reporting.
* Ensure information security risks, audit findings, security incidents, compliance gaps, and remediation commitments have accountable owners, target dates, documented status, and escalation.
* Provide clear, risk-based reporting to executives and governance bodies regarding security operations performance, threat activity, incident response, vulnerability exposure, regulatory readiness, remediation, and resource needs.
* Ensure information security requirements are incorporated into projects, procurements, vendor reviews, architecture decisions, operational changes, clinical workflows, and service transitions.

**IT Project and Portfolio Governance**

* Establish portfolio intake requirements for technology, evaluation, prioritization, sequencing, governance, resource planning, risk management, status reporting, change control, and closure practices.
* Ensure projects have defined sponsorship, scope, outcomes, timelines, budgets, dependencies, operational owners, readiness criteria, and benefit measures.
* Review portfolio health and intervene when technology projects face material schedule, budget, scope, resource, vendor, adoption, or operational-readiness risk.
* Coordinate technology portfolio priorities with the PMO to align with organizational strategy, regulatory commitments, operational capacity, technical roadmaps, information security requirements, and funding.

**IT Vendor, Contract, and Third-Party Governance**

* Lead governance for strategic, high-risk, and operationally significant technology vendors.
* Establish accountable ownership, performance standards, service-review cadence, scorecards, escalation processes, and corrective-action expectations.
* Coordinate technology contract planning, renewals, amendments, statements of work, licensing, support agreements, service levels, and vendor obligations.
* Monitor vendor cost, utilization, performance, support quality, regulatory posture, contractual compliance, lifecycle risk, concentration risk, and value realization.
* Maintain forward visibility into renewals, notice periods, price changes, licensing exposure, implementation commitments, and vendor dependencies.

**Financial, Workforce, and Resource Management**

* Develop and manage assigned operating and capital budgets, forecasts, staffing plans, consulting resources, and contract expenditures.
* Align staffing, vendor capacity, and project resources with demand, organizational priorities, risk, and operational commitments.
* Develop workforce plans, succession considerations, role clarity, cross-training, professional-development priorities, and recruitment strategies.
* Lead, coach, develop, and hold accountable directors, managers, professional staff, consultants, and vendor resources.

**Governance, Performance, and Continuous Improvement**

* Establish an integrated operating rhythm for service performance, information security operations, project delivery, vendor performance, budget, workforce capacity, and improvement initiatives.
* Define measurable goals and key performance indicators; use data to guide decisions and hold leaders and partners accountable.
* Ensure policies, procedures, standards, playbooks, service documentation, knowledge articles, dependency records, and escalation information are current and usable.
* Promote transparent prioritization, consistent decision-making, operational discipline, documentation, and follow-through.

**Other Functions**

* Other duties as assigned.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

* Provides direct leadership to the Information Security Operations leader and the IT Service Senior Manager, and may directly supervise managers, leads, or individual contributors responsible for IT Vendor Management.
* Provides matrixed leadership across technology teams during major incidents, enterprise projects, service transitions, vendor escalations, and material risk response.
* Accountable for workforce planning, performance management, coaching, development, succession planning, and appropriate staffing for assigned functions.

**Additional Details**
**Education, Certifications, and Licenses Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Information Security, Cybersecurity, Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, or a related field.
* An equivalent combination of education and progressively responsible experience may be considered in accordance with organizational requirements.

**Experience Required**

* Ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in information technology, technology operations, service delivery, information security operations, project or portfolio management, vendor management, or a related field.
* Demonstrated experience managing budgets, staffing, contracts, vendors, service levels, operational risk, executive reporting, major incidents, and complex initiatives.

**Preferred Qualifications And Experience**

The

This includes managing Statement of Work (SOW) compliance, operational performance, and quality delivery across nearshore and offshore contact center partners, specifically scheduling operations and offshore administrative and back-office operations.
  
  
This role serves as the primary operational liaison holding vendor leadership accountable to strict Service Level Agreements (SLAs), Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), headcount adherence, and billing reconciliation. The Operations Manager will organize, lead, and drive all vendor governance meeting cadences (weekly, monthly, and quarterly business reviews), manage Corrective Action and Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs), and partner cross-functionally with Workforce Management (WFM), Quality Assurance (QA), IT/Telephony, and Regional Operations to ensure seamless patient experience and cost-efficient operational delivery.
  
  
**You Will**

* SOW & Contract Governance: Manage and enforce all operational terms, deliverables, obligations, and performance benchmarks defined within vendor Statements of Work (SOWs) and Master Services Agreements (MSAs) across all outsourced partners.
* Vendor Accountability & Performance Management: Hold vendor operational leadership strictly accountable for contractual KPIs including Inbound Average Handling Time (IAHT), Call Quality/QA scores, Idle Time, occupancy, adherence, Abandonment Rates, Average Schedule Rate, and Monthly Attrition thresholds (monthly).
* Offshore Administrative Operations Management: Oversee and manage the daily operational workflows, accuracy, turnaround times, and productivity of offshore back-office administrative teams supporting order entry, document administration, medical records requests, insurance validation support, and pre-service tasks.
* Governance Meeting Cadence Leadership: Organize, lead, and establish structured agendas for all recurring vendor governance sessions, including:

+ Weekly Operational & Performance/QC Reviews: Tactical review of SLAs, error trends, and immediate corrective action plans.
+ Weekly Quality Control Calibration: Joint calibration between RadNet and vendor quality teams to ensure consistent evaluation and scoring standards.
+ Weekly Workforce Management (WFM) & Staffing Reviews: Analysis of roster headcount adherence, schedule lock-in, intraday forecasting, and shrinkage mitigation.
+ Weekly Regional Operations Touchpoints: Alignment between regional contact center leaders and dedicated vendor pods.
+ Monthly KPI & Invoice Reconciliation: Audit of monthly billed hours against actual telephony dispositions, validation of penalty deductions, under-staffing fee reductions, and contractual service level credits.

+ Quarterly Business Reviews (QBR): High-level strategic review with executive leadership evaluating operational trends, capacity expansion, technology integration, and overall partnership health.

* Financial & Billing Auditing: Rigorously validate monthly vendor invoices against telephony data (Five9/telephony reports) and approved billable dispositions (Available, Production, Approved Meetings, Approved Nesting/Upskilling). Enforce under-staffing penalty credits, non-billable overages, and downtime limitations for platform outages or local vendor issues.

* Technology & Workflow Integration: Collaborate with internal IT, Telephony, and PMO teams to support vendor access, provisioning, and workflow execution across core RadNet platforms, including Five9 telephony, Salesforce P360, eRAD RIS, and secure enterprise workspaces.
* Training, Onboarding & Nesting Oversight: Partner with internal training teams to ensure vendor new-hire onboarding, 20-day "Ready State" certifications, attrition replacement training (at vendor expense), and compliance training are executed to RadNet standards prior to live production.
* Offshore Compliance & Data Security: Enforce strict adherence to HIPAA, protected health information (PHI) safeguards, ISO/HITRUST security standards, and offshore resource utilization policies in coordination with RadNet Information Security and Compliance.

**If You Are**

Title: Global Digital Workplace and End-User Services Director

Description:
Partners Community Health (PCH) is a new not-for-profit organization, focused on bringing healthcare services together around the needs of people living in Mississauga and West Toronto. PCH currently operates two new state-of the-art LTC homes and community hub in West Mississauga. The new homes have a combined 632-beds and be part of PCH’s larger strategy that introduce innovative and inclusive programs and services and new models of care delivery. PCH is committed to building partnerships and connections that put people first, as well as a learning and leading healthcare community that provides best in class service across the aging continuum.
  
  
Position Summary
  
The Director of Programs, Long-Term Care provides strategic and operational leadership for all resident-focused programs across our long-term care home(s). Reporting to the Executive Director, the Director ensures that programs are person-centred, evidence-informed, and compliant with the Fixing Long-Term Care Act, 2021 and its regulations.
  
The Director leads a multidisciplinary team responsible for delivering high-quality programming in areas such as nursing and personal care, recreation and social engagement, rehabilitation and physiotherapy, restorative care, dementia and palliative supports, and family and community partnerships.
  
A significant component of this role is the strategic and operational oversight of the home's rehabilitation and physiotherapy programs. This includes ensuring the effective delivery of physiotherapy, rehabilitation, restorative care, and mobility services that support residents in maintaining or improving their functional abilities, independence, mobility, and overall quality of life.
  
The Director fosters a culture of dignity, safety, accountability, collaboration, and continuous quality improvement while ensuring that all programs respond to the changing needs, preferences, and goals of residents.
  
Key Responsibilities
  
1. Program Leadership and Strategy
  
  

* Develop, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive program strategy that aligns with the organization's mission, strategic plan, and resident-centred model of care.
* Oversee the planning and delivery of all resident programs, including nursing and personal care, recreation and leisure, spiritual and cultural care, restorative care, rehabilitation and physiotherapy, and palliative and end-of-life supports.
* Identify service gaps and emerging resident needs, and lead the development of new or enhanced programs in collaboration with clinical and interdisciplinary teams.
* Translate best practices, current research, and evidence-informed approaches into practical, measurable program improvements.
* Ensure programs are integrated across departments and contribute to residents' physical, emotional, social, spiritual, and psychological well-being.
* Promote innovative approaches to resident engagement, functional independence, rehabilitation, and quality of life.

2. Rehabilitation and Physiotherapy Program Oversight
  
  

* Provide strategic and operational leadership and oversight of the home's rehabilitation and physiotherapy programs, ensuring effective delivery of resident-centred rehabilitation services.
* Oversee physiotherapy, occupational therapy, restorative care, and other rehabilitation services, as applicable, ensuring programs are aligned with residents' assessed needs, individualized care plans, and functional goals.
* Ensure residents receive timely assessments, individualized treatment plans, ongoing reassessments, and appropriate rehabilitation interventions to maintain or improve mobility, strength, balance, range of motion, and functional independence.
* Monitor the quality, effectiveness, and accessibility of rehabilitation and physiotherapy services, using measurable outcomes to evaluate program performance and resident progress.
* Work collaboratively with nursing, personal support workers, recreation, dietary, and other interdisciplinary team members to integrate rehabilitation goals into residents' daily care and routines.
* Provide leadership and direction to rehabilitation and physiotherapy personnel, ensuring appropriate staffing, scheduling, performance management, and professional development.
* Oversee rehabilitation resources, equipment, service contracts, and operational processes to ensure effective and efficient program delivery.
* Ensure appropriate documentation, communication, and follow-up regarding rehabilitation assessments, treatment plans, interventions, and resident outcomes.
* Identify opportunities to enhance restorative care and rehabilitation programming, including falls prevention, mobility maintenance, functional improvement, and strategies to reduce avoidable functional decline.
* Ensure rehabilitation and physiotherapy services comply with applicable legislation, professional practice standards, Ministry of Long-Term Care requirements, and organizational policies.
* Promote ongoing education and development of staff to support safe mobility, proper transfer techniques, restorative approaches, and rehabilitation principles throughout the home.

3. Quality, Compliance, and Risk Management
  
  

* Ensure all programs comply with the Fixing Long-Term Care Act, 2021, Ontario Regulation 246/22, Ministry of Long-Term Care requirements, and other applicable legislation and standards.
* Lead required program evaluations, annual reviews, and continuous quality improvement (CQI) initiatives, tracking outcomes through key quality indicators.
* Prepare for and respond to Ministry inspections, complaints, critical incidents, and accreditation reviews, including the development and monitoring of compliance action plans.
* Oversee infection prevention and control, falls prevention, responsive behaviours, skin and wound care, pain management, rehabilitation, restorative care, and other required clinical programs.
* Monitor and evaluate rehabilitation and physiotherapy program outcomes, including resident functional improvement, mobility, falls, and maintenance of activities of daily living.
* Ensure rehabilitation and physiotherapy programs are incorporated into the home's continuous quality improvement initiatives and annual program evaluations.
* Monitor compliance with applicable professional practice standards and ensure rehabilitation services are delivered safely and in accordance with residents' individualized care plans.

Title: Director, Project Management
Description:
Everest Clinical Research (“Everest”) is a full-service contract research organization (CRO) providing a broad range of expertise-based clinical research services to worldwide pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device industries. We serve some of the best-known companies and work with many of the most advanced drugs, biologics, and medical devices in development today.

Everest has been an independent CRO since 2004 with a strong foundation as a statistical and data management center of excellence. Building on this foundation, Everest has successfully developed and established itself as a full-service CRO. Everest’s Corporate headquarters are located in Ontario, Canada and US headquarters in New Jersey, USA, with additional physical offices in Asia and Europe.

Everest is known in the industry for its high-quality deliverables, superior customer service, and flexibility in meeting clients’ needs. A dynamic organization with an entrepreneurial origin, Everest continues to experience exceptional growth and great success.

Quality is our backbone, customer-focus is our tradition, flexibility is our strength…that’s us…that’s Everest.

To drive continued success in this exciting clinical research field, we are seeking a committed, skilled, and customer-focused individual to join our winning team as a **Director, Project Management** for our Toronto/Markham, Ontario, Canada on-site location, or remotely from a home-based office anywhere in Canada in accordance with our Work from Home policy.

**Director, Project Management:**

This leadership role will oversee the project planning, communication, and execution of clinical research and development services offered by Everest. Direct reports include all levels and roles within the Project Management department, including Associate Directors, Senior Managers, Managers, Senior Project Managers, Project Managers, Associate Project Managers and Project Coordinators. In-direct reports/subordinates are those Project Managers who are assigned to the tasks on the client studies and projects overseen by the Director of Project Management (matrixed organization).

**JOB ACCOUNTABILITIES:**

* Plan and implement new client service delivery requests within client portfolio; support evolution of existing client portfolio, providing holistic biometrics and full services (including clinical operations) project deliveries across multiple clinical development programs.
* Strategically align the efforts of functional area directors and managers in project planning, identification of tasks and deliverables, and assessment of resource needs and utilization for existing and new clients/sponsors.
* Perform project and portfolio performance tracking for responsible projects using strategic planning and project tracking methods and tools. Conduct regular project progress reviews with internal teams for assigned portfolios, and facilitate conduct of Everest and Client governance meetings to optimize partnership expectations and performance.
* Check and ensure that responsible projects carried out at Everest are properly tracked and managed according to Everest’s quality, operational and financial budget standards. Support solution and budget development for complex and unique projects and scope to address client requirements.
* Provide leadership, training, mentorship, and management oversight of project management staff. This may include mentorship and training of team members to deliver project management services for specific client portfolios, or mentorship and career development of individuals in a line management capacity.
* In consultation with the senior Project Management leadership, review new Project Management Applicants and recommend hires for interview processing.
* In consultation with the senior Project Management leadership, further develop and establish policies and Standard Operating Procedures in project management for assurance of quality deliverables. Continue to support the development, update, and review of governing documents and WIs for the department.
* Initiate, drive, and support project management departmental process and technology improvement initiatives. Lead and contribute to developing reusable project management templates and training materials that can be used to improve effectiveness and efficiency of project delivery by other team members.
* Through the periodic project/portfolio review meetings, effectively identify issues such as lack of planning, lack of resources, poor team performance, or other external factors negatively impacting the ongoing projects, and bring the issues and solutions to the attention of the functional area directors and managers. Work with the functional area directors and managers to jointly ensure smooth project starting up, continuation, and successful completion.
* In consultation with Everest functional leaders and senior project management leadership, interact with clients for strategic partnership governance activities, which includes but is not limited to project pipeline and delivery planning, measuring performance metrics for the portfolio, identifying new project/service opportunities within the existing portfolio, implementing performance improvement and innovation initiatives, and obtaining key information to aid in the projection of resource requirements and project management purposes.
* Manage all project management aspects of assigned Phase I -IV clinical trials and in accordance with ICH guidelines, FDA, Health Canada, EMA, and other applicable regulatory and legal requirements.
* Lead cross-functional project teams. Manage the planning, implementation, conduct, and reporting of assigned projects within the established timelines and budgets, and with the quality and requirements necessary for regulatory approvals.
* Proactively track and manage project tasks against timelines and hours spent/budgets, alert management when there are risks of having major deviations. Proactively track and manage the financial status against budget and reconcile expenses across sub-streams of activities.
* Function as senior level facilitator of problem solving and conflict resolution, and act as a 2nd level escalation resource.
* Conduct “lessons learned” meetings with project team members to learn from failures and prevent same from future projects.
* Contribute and/or participate in the performance evaluation of staff who performed under the responsible projects.
* When required, this position may assist the organization in responding to and preparing for RFI and RFPs, and subsequently leading and participating in bid defense meetings, defining work scopes and budgets, and leading contract administration activities.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* B.Sc. or M.Sc. in life sciences or health related field.
* A minimum of 18 years of experience in clinical research and development within a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, institutional, or CRO setting.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and develop others within functional area.
* Demonstrated understanding of cross-functional processes including clinical operations, statistics, data management, pharmacovigilance, subject randomization and drug supply management, data monitoring and adjudication committees, regulatory affairs, and medical writing.
* Knowledge and understanding of ICH guidelines, FDA, Health Canada, and EMA regulations.
* Ability to define scopes and estimate budgets, plan and manage projects, including resource requirements and utilization, hours spent vs. budgets, key deliverables and timelines.
* Demonstrated leadership abilities, including setting goals for others and driving to achieve them in accordance with allocated resources, timelines, and budgets.
* Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills. Demonstrated strong negotiation and presentation skills.
* Strong ability in problem-solving, including conflict resolution.

  

**Benefits & Compensation:**

We offer a robust benefits package to support your health, well-being, and growth, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, life & AD&D insurance, short- and long-term disability, tuition reimbursement, fitness reimbursement, employee assistance program (EAP), a pension plan, generous paid time off and sick leave, and the opportunity to earn a performance based bonus.

To find out more about Everest Clinical Research and to review other opportunities, please visit our website at www.everestclinical.com (http://www.ecrscorp.com).

* Experience supporting the operations of an office, business unit, or portfolio of projects.
* Experience with project financial performance, resource forecasting, utilization management, and operational reporting.

* Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across technical disciplines and business functions.

Title: Senior Manager, Inside Delivery
Description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it's a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn't been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

#### **What you'll do**

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

* Creating a strategic roadmap and services architecture for how Scout Motors will sell and transact new and used vehicles to retail customers, from purchase through delivery.
* Supporting and driving the definition and design of the ideal transaction process from an operational perspective (documentation, information flows, and third-party integrations).
* Leading vehicle registration compliance efforts across all active and future sales markets, including program build-out, process design, and cross-functional enablement.
* Developing and documenting comprehensive knowledge of vehicle sales and registration requirements across all states, counties, and localities.
* Designing and operationalizing transaction and delivery workflows and an efficient operating model that ensures a scalable, reliable, customer-centric experience.
* Partnering closely with product managers and engineers to translate operational needs into requirements, prioritize improvements, and develop scalable tools and vendor integrations for end-to-end vehicle sales transactions and deliveries, including documentation, payments, financing, registration, and delivery readiness.
* Leading the operational implementation of AI and automation across the transaction and delivery journey, identifying practical use cases that reduce manual work, improve document accuracy, and help customers complete their purchase and prepare for delivery.
* Owning business testing, rollout, and team adoption of new tools, with clear escalation paths and appropriate human review; measuring impact on transaction completion time, accuracy, team productivity, and the customer experience to guide ongoing improvements.
* Creating a technical support model for sales transaction workflows and operating models.
* Coordinating with Finance to define and build systems that accurately recognize vehicle revenue, ensuring alignment between operations and financial reporting.
* Participating in vendor evaluations and providing operational insight for standard operating procedures, transaction policies, and retail training.

**Location & Travel Expectations**:

* This role will be based out of the **Scout Motors corporate headquarters in Charlotte, NC**.
* This role requires 4 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.
* Applicants should expect that the role will require the ability to convene with Scout colleagues in person and travel to participate in events on behalf of the company from time to time.

#### **What you'll bring**

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You'll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You'll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

* Bachelor's degree in a relevant field.
* 10+ years experience managing automotive sales transactions.
* Deep technical acumen and comprehensive regulatory knowledge, especially in vehicle registration and titling requirements.
* Proven experience in early-stage companies: building teams, policies, tools, and pivoting from design to operational execution.
* Experience implementing AI or automation in operational workflows and working closely with product managers and engineers to deliver scalable tools and measurable improvements in efficiency, accuracy, and customer experience.
* Proven ability to lead and motivate cross-functional teams, with a focus on fostering a positive and inclusive work environment.
* Collaborative mindset and ability to bring together both internal and external teams behind a common vision; skillful at organizational navigation and cross-functional collaboration at all levels; ability to develop effective partnerships and relationships.
* High agency with capability to independently solve problems and develop strategic, sustainable solutions.
* Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and meet deadlines.

#### **What you'll gain**

The benefits of joining Scout include the chance to build products and a company from the ground up. This is a chance to create something new and lasting – with an iconic brand at its foundation. In addition, Scout provides competitive compensation and benefits to support your physical, mental, and financial wellbeing. Program specifics are detailed in company policies and employee benefit guides, select highlights:

* Competitive insurance including:
  + Medical, dental, vision and income protection plans
* 401(k) program with:
  + An employer match and immediate vesting
* Generous Paid Time Off including:
  + 20 days planned PTO, as accrued
  + 40 hours of unplanned PTO and 14 company or floating holidays, annually
  + Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave for biological and adoptive parents of all genders
  + Paid leave for circumstances related to bereavement, jury duty, voting time, or military leave
* Corporate Vehicle Program with:
  + Eligibility for 1 assigned vehicle
  + A mobility stipend

#### **Pay Transparency**

This is a full-time, exempt position eligible to receive a base salary and to participate in an annual performance bonus program. Final salary offered will be determined based on factors including but not limited to the candidate's skills and experience. The annual performance bonus program is preset and not candidate dependent.

Initial base salary range = $150,000.00 - $181,250.00

Internal leveling code: M7

* To be considered for career opportunities at Scout Motors, applicants must be 18 years of age or older.
* Residing in **San Francisco**: *Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Scout Motors will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.*

**Equal Opportunity**

Scout Motors is committed to employing a diverse workforce and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, disability, pregnancy, or any other characteristics protected by law. Scout Motors is committed to compliance with all applicable fair employment practice laws. If you require reasonable accommodation to complete a job application, pre-employment testing, or a job interview or to otherwise participate in the hiring process, please contact ScoutAccommodations@scoutmotors.com.

Title: VP, Operations & Patient Experience
Description:
**About Us**

LifeMD is a leading provider of virtual primary care, telehealth, and specialized treatment programs serving hundreds of thousands of patients nationwide. Our vertically integrated platform combines 50-state licensed providers, in-house pharmacy and lab integrations, and proprietary technology that enables safe, high-quality, and affordable care.

At the heart of this transformation is our team of developers, engineers, and tech innovators building state-of-the-art systems that make healthcare smarter, faster, and more accessible. From architecting scalable backend systems to crafting intuitive user experiences, we are pushing boundaries every day.

Recognized as one of the fastest-growing healthcare tech companies (#166 on Deloitte Fast 500 in 2023), LifeMD is not just a healthcare company — it's a tech company revolutionizing healthcare.

**About the Role**

The VP, Operations & Patient Experience leads the teams that deliver care and support to every LifeMD patient. The role oversees about 150 people across clinical support operations (medical assistants, scheduling and clinical program management), the patient care center (customer service, care navigation, sales and quality assurance), and the operations function that keeps the business running (program management, procurement and inventory).

The VP serves as the central hub connecting every part of the business to the patient. Delivering high-quality care depends on ongoing collaboration with marketing, technology, finance, pharmacy and LifeMD's affiliated medical group: aligning patient support capacity with marketing's acquisition and retention plans, shaping the product and technology roadmap around what patients and care teams need, partnering with finance on budgets, KPIs and unit economics, and working with pharmacy and providers so every patient's care, from visit to medication, is seamless.

This is a hands-on operating role for a leader who has run clinical operations at scale. In the coming year, the priorities are using AI and automation to raise productivity across patient support, optimizing every patient touchpoint from onboarding through ongoing care, and lowering the cost of serving each patient.

**Responsibilities**

**Cross-functional Partnership**

* Act as the operational hub between patient-facing teams and the rest of the business, so decisions across every function account for their impact on patient care.
* Partner with marketing on demand forecasts, launches and retention programs, so staffing and support are ready for every patient.
* Partner with technology and product to prioritize platform, workflow and AI improvements based on what patients and care teams need.
* Partner with finance on budgets, operational KPIs and unit economics.
* Partner with LifeMD's pharmacy on fulfillment, shipping and refills, so patients receive their medications reliably and on time.
* Partner with LifeMD's affiliated medical group (PC) on clinical workflows, quality and handoffs between providers and care teams, so care delivery and patient support work as one.

**Clinical Operations**

* Lead clinical support operations, including medical assistants, scheduling and clinical program management.
* Partner with medical group leadership on provider capacity, utilization and coverage across sync and async care.
* Manage clinical vendor relationships, contracts and transitions.

**AI and Automation**

* Lead the adoption of AI and automation across patient support and clinical workflows, including AI agents in the patient care center.
* Measure the impact of each deployment on productivity, quality and cost.

**Cost and Unit Economics**

* Own the operations budget and deliver against annual cost targets.
* Drive down the cost of serving each patient through workforce planning, productivity standards and vendor rationalization.
* Set and report operational KPIs in partnership with finance.

**Patient Care Center and Experience**

* Set the strategy and direction for the patient care center (customer service, care navigation, sales and quality assurance), working through its senior director and director, who lead the teams day to day.
* Own patient experience metrics such as resolution, response times and satisfaction, and partner with the business GMs on the on-therapy patient experience.

**Operations and Program Management**

* Run the program management office for cross-functional initiatives, keeping work on schedule and surfacing bottlenecks early.
* Oversee procurement and inventory.

**Leadership**

* Lead and develop a team of directors and senior managers, building a strong leadership bench.
* Represent operations and patient experience with the executive team and with external vendors and partners.

  
**Requirements**  

* 10+ years of operations experience, including 5+ years leading multi-layer operations teams (leaders of managers) with large hourly or clinical support workforces.
* Senior leadership experience in healthcare clinical operations, ideally in virtual care, telehealth or a multi-state provider group.
* Hands-on experience deploying AI or automation in operations, with measurable results.
* Proven cost discipline: has owned a large operating budget and reduced costs without sacrificing quality or patient experience.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, including with executive and board audiences.

**Preferred**

* A clinical background, such as RN, NP or PA, or a clinical operations leadership track.
* Experience leading a contact center at scale.
* Familiarity with multi-state licensing and the regulatory environment for virtual care.

  
**Benefits**  

* Salary: $200,000-250,000 + 15% bonus
* Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
* Retirement Plan (401k, Roth 401k)
* Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary & AD&D)
* Paid Time Off
* Paid Holidays
* Short Term Disability
* Training & Development

Title: Senior Manager, Customer Billing Operations
Description:
**Join the Clean Energy Revolution**

  

Lead a critical Customer Billing Operations (CBO) organization responsible for delivering timely, accurate, and compliant billing for Southern California Edison (SCE) customers. As **Senior Manager**, you will lead frontline leaders and operational teams, drive performance across key billing and service commitments, strengthen operational controls and workforce capability, and partner across the organization to resolve complex operational challenges. You will also provide operational leadership through significant change as CBO advances automation, Operational Excellence, AMI 2.0, and other future-state initiatives.

  

As a **Senior Manager, Customer Billing Operations**, your work will help power our planet, reduce carbon emissions and create cleaner air for everyone. Are you ready to take on the challenge to help us build the future?

  

**Incident Management Team Expected Participation**: Employees are expected to support emergency response and/or business continuity efforts, including readiness to serve on an Incident Management Team (IMT) when needed. Employees will participate in an on-call rotation (approximately every four to six weeks), to support IMT activations during emergency events. IMT assignments may differ from an individual’s regular responsibilities.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Develops and implements business operating plans which align with Operating Unit or enterprise business strategy and short, medium-term objectives.
* Develops and implements business operations risk management strategies.
* Leads the prioritization of strategic planning scenarios which effectively address business challenges while successfully achieving operational performance metrics.
* Defines business metrics, evaluates impact of new and existing initiatives, and initiates and implements changes to improve ongoing operations.
* Administers projects including planning, strategizing, coordination, implementation and quality control. Designs project management systems/tools to facilitate work processes, records management, and communications.
* Oversees the undertaking of data gathering for the development of strategies based upon the market. Oversees the allocation of resources, ensures delivery of sufficient support to a business function.
* A material job duty of all positions within the Company is ensuring the protection of all its physical, financial and cybersecurity assets, and properly accessing and managing private customer data, proprietary information, confidential medical records, and other types of highly sensitive information and data with the highest standards of conduct and integrity.

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------

* Five or more years of experience supervising a team of direct reports and/or project management.
* Experience in leading business operations analysis.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Eight or more years of progressively responsible experience in customer operations, billing operations, utility operations, financial operations, or another complex transaction-based operational environment.
* Five or more years of experience with utility billing, customer operations, meter-to-cash processes, SAP IS-U, BPEMs, tariffs, SOX requirements, regulatory requirements, or comparable regulated customer operations.
* Experience managing vendor or third-party operational relationships in a service-delivery.
* Lean Six Sigma, Project Management Professional (PMP), change-management, or comparable operational/process-improvement certification.
* Experience managing complex operational performance across measures such as backlog, aging, cycle time, quality, productivity, accuracy, service levels, customer outcomes, or other key performance indicators.
* Experience developing and executing operational strategies, performance-recovery plans, corrective actions, and continuous-improvement initiatives that deliver measurable and sustainable results.
* Experience managing operations within a regulated environment with accountability for compliance, audit readiness, quality assurance, risk management, and internal controls.
* Experience leading workforce planning, employee development, talent management, succession planning, organizational effectiveness, and employee-engagement activities.
* Experience leading organizations through significant technology, regulatory, process, or organizational change while maintaining day-to-day operational performance.
* Experience partnering across organizations such as Customer Service, Information Technology, Compliance, Account Management, Vendor Management, Finance, Regulatory, or Operational Excellence to resolve issues and deliver shared priorities.
* Experience leading or sponsoring automation, technology modernization, operational transformation, business-readiness, or continuous-improvement initiatives.
* Ability to develop strategic plans, annual objectives, operational roadmaps, performance measures, and governance routines that drive accountability and results.
* Strong executive communication and influencing skills, including experience presenting operational performance, risks, recommendations, transformation priorities, and strategic plans to senior leadership.

  

**Additional Information**

* This position’s work mode is **hybrid.** The employee will report to an SCE facility for a set number of days with the option to work remotely on the remaining days. Unless otherwise noted, employees are required to work and reside in the state of California. Further details of this work mode will be discussed at the interview stage. The work mode can be changed based on business needs.
* Visit our Candidate Resource page to get meaningful information related to benefits, perks, resources, testing information, hiring process, and more!
* Qualified applications with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act.
  

**About Southern California Edison**

  

The people at SCE don't just keep the lights on. Our mission is so much bigger. We’re fueling the kind of innovation that’s changing an entire industry, and quite possibly the planet. Join us and create a future with cleaner energy, while providing our customers with the safety and reliability they demand. At SCE, you’ll have a chance to grow personally and professionally, making a real impact in Southern California and around the world.

Title: Call Center Operations Manager
Description:
**About BlinkRx:**

BlinkRx is rebuilding how Americans access life-changing medicines. Today, only one in five prescriptions for new branded therapies are ever filled. The problem isn't the medicine. It's insurance barriers, affordability challenges, fragmented pharmacy experiences, and inadequate support that keep patients from starting and staying on treatment. Our mission is to change that.

We built RxOS, the first AI-powered prescription operating system. RxOS connects the largest network of doctors, patients, pharmacies, payers, and pharmaceutical manufacturers, intelligently orchestrating every step to guarantee a seamless prescription journey for every script.

Our teams solve complex, high-stakes problems at the intersection of artificial intelligence, healthcare operations, logistics, payments, and regulation. The impact is transformative: BlinkRx more than doubles the rate at which patients take their medications and lowers their out-of-pocket expenses by hundreds of dollars every month.

BlinkRx created and leads a rapidly growing $80+ billion category, with exceptional momentum:

* **Built for scale:**
  Over the past decade, we have invested nearly $1 billion in building the technology and operational platform required to serve patients at scale.
* **Proven growth and economics:**
  We have grown 100% annually for the past five years, are profitable, and support more than 60 pharmaceutical brands.
* **Trusted with category-defining programs:**
  Our technology powers a leading pharmaceutical manufacturer’s direct-to-patient platform for its GLP-1 portfolio, providing the infrastructure to expand patient access as demand for these therapies grows.

We are a dynamic team of technologists and industry experts seeking to build a generational company that delivers a genuine step change in American health.

**The Role:**
The Patient Services Operations team is at the forefront of the company mission to bring affordable prices and deliver the best possible experience for all of our customers. As a Call Center Operations Manager, you won't just oversee a team — you'll set the pace, raise the bar, and build a culture where grit and customer obsession are the standard, not the exception. This is a high-intensity, high-impact role. You'll combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution: designing systems that scale, coaching talent that sticks, and using data to drive relentless improvement. When things break — and in a fast-growing company, things break — you'll be the one who figures it out and moves the team forward. You'll collaborate across product, engineering, pharmacy, and business leadership to translate the voice of the customer into real operational and product changes. This is not a role for someone who wants to manage from a distance.

***This is a full-time, on-site position based in our Pittsburgh (Robinson Twp.) office.***

**What you’ll do:**

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of customer service reps and team leads — holding the bar high while investing in each person's growth.
* Drive a performance culture built on accountability, candid feedback, and real development — not just annual reviews.
* Create an environment where people do their best work, feel ownership over outcomes, and genuinely care about the patients they serve.

**Operational Management**

* Own the day-to-day: ensure timely, high-quality resolution of customer issues across all channels (phone, email, chat) — at speed and at scale.
* Tackle complex, ambiguous escalations head-on with sound judgment and customer-first instincts.
* Build and enforce policies, processes, and SLAs that are rigorous but human — protecting the customer experience while enabling a fast-moving team.
* Stay ahead of capacity: monitor workload, adjust staffing, and anticipate surges before they become fires.

**Performance Monitoring & Reporting**

* Own the metrics that matter — CSAT, NPS, FCR, response time, resolution time — and use them to tell a story, not just report numbers.
* Surface trends in customer behavior and pain points; turn those insights into action with product, engineering, and operations.
* Implement Quality Assurance programs that raise the floor on service quality, every week.

**Process Improvement**

* Relentlessly question the status quo: identify friction in workflows, eliminate steps that slow agents down, and reduce customer effort at every touchpoint.
* Lead improvement initiatives end-to-end — design, pilot, measure, iterate.
* Bring the customer's voice to cross-functional teams, ensuring it shapes product decisions and business strategy.

**Technology & Tools**

* Evaluate, implement, and optimize CRM, ticketing, and support tooling — with a bias toward automation and efficiency.
* Partner with engineering and vendor teams to push system enhancements that keep our support infrastructure ahead of our growth curve.
* Treat data integrity as non-negotiable: if the data isn't clean, the decisions aren't sound.

**A successful applicant will fit the following criteria:**

We want someone who runs toward hard things. You'll thrive here if:

* You have 5+ years of leadership experience in fast-paced, high-volume customer service or call center environments.
* You have 2+ years in customer service, healthcare, pharmacy, or a related field — you understand the stakes when a patient can't get their medication.
* You're a builder of teams and systems — not just a manager of tasks.
* You use data instinctively: you know which metrics to watch, how to find the story in the numbers, and how to translate insights into action.
* You thrive in ambiguity. When priorities shift (and they will), you recalibrate fast and keep the team grounded.
* You communicate with clarity and conviction — up, down, and across the org — and you do it with respect and patience.
* You have a low ego and a high standard. You'll do whatever it takes, including jumping on the phones when the team needs it.
* Spanish bilingual is preferred — for supporting diverse customers and teams.
* You have a bachelor's degree in Business, Communications, or equivalent real-world experience.

**Why Join Us:**
It is rare to have a company that both deeply impacts its customers and is able to provide its services across a massive population.  At Blink, we have a huge impact on people when they are most vulnerable: at the intersection of their healthcare and finances. We are also the fastest growing healthcare company in the country and are driving that impact across millions of new patients every year.  Our business model not only helps people, but drives economics that allow us to build a generational company. We are a relentlessly learning, constantly curious, and aggressively collaborative cross-functional team dedicated to inventing new ways to improve the lives of our customers.
  
  
We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity of all kinds. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
  
  
Applicants who provide their phone number and consent to receive text messages may receive SMS or MMS updates from Blink Health regarding their application.
